Details

Mission and objectives

The UN Resident Coordinator’s Office (UN RCO) in Nepal works under the strategic guidance of the UN Resident Coordinator (RC) and supports the UN Country Team (UNCT) in the advancement of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. The UN RCO fulfills the following five key functions in support of the responsibilities of the RC and the UNCT including: Strategic planning; Development economics; Partnerships and development finance; Data and results management and reporting; and Research, communications and advocacy. The UN RCO and UNCT work closely with the Government of Nepal and other Development Partners to support Nepal in achieving Agenda 2030 and the Sustainable Development Goals. The UN RCO team supports the RC and UNCT in ensuring a more coordinated and coherent approach across the work of the UN and is composed of experts in development and humanitarian coordination, information management, human rights, gender equality, communications and communications.

Context

The UN Resident Coordinator is the highest-ranking representative of the UN development system in Nepal and leads the UN Country Team (UNCT) of resident and non-resident agencies, funds and programmes. The Resident Coordinator’s Office supports the Resident Coordinator in steering the delivery of the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) 2023 to 2027, agreed with the Government of Nepal, and in coordinating the UN’s collective response to national priorities, including disaster response, Nepal’s transition out of the least developed country category, climate action and the 2030 Agenda. The RCO’s communications function positions the UN as one coherent partner to the Government and the people of Nepal. It supports the Resident Coordinator’s public voice, produces joint UNCT content and chairs the UN Communications Group (UNCG), which brings together communications focal points from across the UN system in Nepal. Nepal’s audiences are young and mobile-first. Reaching them requires content that is made for vertical screens, published in Nepali as well as English, and produced at the speed of the platforms. This assignment brings a young Nepali creator into the RCO to strengthen that capacity and to keep the UN’s digital presence current, credible and genuinely watchable.

Task description

Under the supervision of the National Information Officer, the UN Volunteer will produce original digital content for UN Nepal’s social media channels, maintain the joint content calendar, and support campaigns and live coverage of UNCT events. The UN Volunteer will contribute a young audience perspective to communications planning and will build practical creative skills in a multilateral working environment

. A. Content production

  • Produce short-form vertical video(reels) for UNCT Nepal channels, covering concept, script, filming, editing, subtitling, sound and export in platform-native formats.
  • Design static and animated assets, including carousels, quote cards, infographics and event graphics, in line with the UNCT visual identity and UN Nepal brand guidance.
  • Write platform-tailored copy in Nepali and English, adjusting register and length for each channel rather than reposting a single text across all of them.
  • Cover Resident Coordinator and UNCT events, launches and joint events as photographer and videographer, and deliver same-day clips and images where required.
  •  Source and produce human-interest content with agency communications colleagues, showing how UN support reaches people, with informed consent obtained and recorded for every person featured.
  •  Maintain the RCO digital asset library, including captions, credits, consent records and version control.

B. Channel management and engagement

  •  Maintain and update the UN Nepal content calendar across Facebook, X, Instagram, LinkedIn, YouTube and TikTok, aligned to the UNSDCF, international days and joint UNCT moments.
  •  Schedule and publish approved content, and monitor comments and direct messages during agreed hours.
  •  Draft responses to routine audience queries, and escalate sensitive, political or reputational matters to the supervisor without responding directly.
  •  Monitor conversation and sentiment on UN-related topics in Nepali digital spaces, and flag misinformation for verification and coordinated response.
  •  Support live coverage of high-visibility events, including real-time posting and rapid-turnaround edits.

C. Campaigns and joint UN work

  •  Contribute creative concepts for content to joint UN campaigns and international day observances, and produce the assets agreed for each.
  • Support the UNCG with shared content packages, including toolkits that agencies can adapt for their own channels.
  • Support youth-facing initiatives such as reel competitions, creator collaborations, vox pop series and campus activations.
  • Support the digital rollout of RCO publications, including the UNCT Results Report and the UN Nepal newsletter.

  • Compile monthly performance analytics across platforms, with plain-language interpretation of what worked and what did not.
  •  Test formats, posting times and narrative approaches, and document findings so they inform the following month’s calendar.
  • Contribute inputs on communications results to RCO reporting.

  • Share editing, design and platform skills with UNCG colleagues through short peer learning sessions.
  •  Maintain awareness of platform and format shifts relevant to UN Nepal’s audiences and advise accordingly.

By the end of the assignment, the following are expected:

  • Demonstrable growth in engagement and reach on UN Nepal channels against the baseline set in the first month.

As a global leader, CARE is shaping the future of the humanitarian and development sector. Each year, we deliver support and services to millions of people in over a hundred countries. We do this by focusing on our mission and living the values that drive our organization. A career at CARE is an opportunity to be part of a movement that brings communities together to solve complex problems and foster lasting change throughout the world. We seek individuals who are passionate about humanitarian and development work, collaborate well with others, embrace learning and innovation, and deliver results.

CARE has been operational in Nepal since 1978 and works in partnerships with government and non-government stakeholders across the spectrum of humanitarian action and long-term development programs. We create local solutions to poverty and inequality and seek dignity for everyone every day and during times of crisis. CARE puts women and girls at the center of everything we do because they have proven to be the best hope for creating lasting change in the world.

What it’s like to work at CARE?

CARE is a mission-driven international humanitarian aid and development organization that offers an opportunity to work with people across the world. Not a day will go by that you won’t learn something profound, meet an expert, or write a sentence that can change a life. We are committed to an environment where everyone can succeed.

The Bhotekoshi flash floods caused widespread damage and displacement across the affected districts of Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha, Tanahun, and Chitwan. The disaster severely disrupted shelter, livelihoods, WASH services, and access to essential services, while also increasing protection, gender, and social inclusion risks for affected communities.

CDM-Nepal is a leading non-governmental development and humanitarian organisation of Lumbini Province of Nepal. Established in 2000 in Butwal, CDM-Nepal has worked in DRM, CCA, WASH, livelihood and GBV. CDM’s programmes have historically been targeted at underprivileged women and children. Origins of CDM-Nepal CDM-Nepal’s origin can be traced back to 1993, the year Rupandehi district experienced one of the devastating floods in its history. Having seen the havoc brought by the disaster, a group of local development professionals joined hands to informally set up “Save the Environment and Rural Development Institute (SERDI)”, which later became CDM-Nepal during official registration in 2000.

Vision: Our vision is to make just, equitable, peaceful, prosperous and disaster-resilient society for all citizens of Nepal.

Mission: Our mission is to improve the lives of individuals and families in the poorest, vulnerable, socially excluded and marginalised communities of Nepal.

Objectives: Reduce – Contribute to substantially reduce disaster risk and losses in lives, livelihoods and health and the economic, physical, social, cultural and environmental assets of persons, businesses, communities and countries

IMPROVE: Improve socio-economic status of the poor, marginalized and vulnerable sections of the community by implementing risk-informed, gender-responsive and inclusive livelihood improvement, health, WASH and education programmes with a rights-based perspective

PARTNERSHIP: Partner with local, Province and Central governments, Development Partner and civil society organisations for programme design, implementation and evaluation

LEARNING: Generate learning through applied research on relevant socio-economic, climate, disaster and environmental issues and utilise learning for advocacy and also utilize for organisational development

GOVERNANCE – Advocate and campaign at the local, province and national levels to address the root causes of development challenges

Summary:

Project HOPE is seeking a WASH Technical Advisor to support its emergency response to landslides and flooding in Nepal. The consultant will provide technical guidance and support for the design, implementation, monitoring, and coordination of emergency WASH activities serving affected communities and supporting health delivery points.

The consultant will work closely with Project HOPE’s emergency response and program teams, local partners, government authorities, WASH Cluster actors, and other humanitarian organizations. The consultant will provide technical recommendations, monitor progress and water quality, support coordination, and identify and address challenges affecting WASH activities.

Scope of Consultancy

The consultant will provide services in the following areas:

  • Provide technical guidance on emergency WASH activities, including water supply, sanitation, hygiene promotion, water trucking, and water quality monitoring.
  • Support the design, implementation, and rehabilitation of water systems, as appropriate to the emergency context.
  • Monitor WASH activities and provide recommendations and mitigation measures to address implementation challenges.
  • Conduct and document water quality testing associated with water trucking, water distribution, and other relevant WASH activities.
  • Support the integration of WASH activities with health, gender, protection, nutrition, and other relevant humanitarian sectors.
  • Coordinate with government authorities, WASH Cluster actors, UN agencies, NGOs, local implementing partners, and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Provide technical input to WASH-related planning, procurement, budgeting, partner activities, monitoring, and reporting.
  • Participate in relevant coordination meetings and provide regular technical updates to the Emergency Response Team.
  • Support monitoring of WASH-related partner deliverables and identify and flag implementation, performance, or compliance concerns.
  • Provide technical input to internal and donor reporting related to WASH activities.

Expected Outputs

During the consultancy period, the consultant is expected to contribute and deliver the following:

  • Effective technical oversight and support for implementation of emergency WASH activities in Nepal.
  • Regular monitoring of WASH activities, including water trucking, water distribution, water quality testing, and hygiene-related interventions.
  • Timely identification of WASH-related challenges, with practical recommendations and mitigation measures provided to the Emergency Response Team.
  • Regular technical updates and reporting on WASH activities, progress, challenges, and priorities.
  • Effective coordination with government authorities, WASH Cluster actors, humanitarian organizations, local partners, and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Support technical input to WASH-related planning, procurement, budgeting, partner activities, and reporting.
  • Documentation of water quality testing and other relevant WASH monitoring data.
  • Technical recommendations to support quality, accountability, and alignment of WASH activities with applicable humanitarian standards, including Sphere standards.
  • Detailed deliverables, timelines, and performance expectations will be agreed upon with the consultant and documented as part of the consultancy engagement.

Duration of Assignment: Approximately 1 month

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in water and sanitation engineering, civil engineering, or a related WASH technical field.
  • At least 5 years of experience designing and implementing emergency WASH programs, preferably in humanitarian, IDP, refugee, or migrant settings.
  • Experience with water supply systems, sanitation, hygiene promotion, water quality testing, and WASH activities in or around health facilities.
  • Experience working in emergency and early recovery contexts.
  • Knowledge of Sphere standards and humanitarian WASH practices.
  • Experience coordinating with government authorities, humanitarian organizations, partners, and WASH Cluster actors.
  • Experience with WASH monitoring, reporting, proposal development, and/or donor reporting.
  • Strong communication and coordination skills.
  • Experience working in Nepal or a similar humanitarian emergency context.
  • Experience integrating WASH with health, gender, protection, and other humanitarian sectors.
  • Experience working with local implementing partners and supporting WASH-related procurement and activity planning.
  • Fluency in Nepali and working proficiency in English are required.

The consultancy fee will be determined based on the scope of services, qualifications, and experience of the selected consultant.

Notice to applicants: Project HOPE does not conduct direct solicitation/recruitment via email. Project HOPE never asks consultant applicants for payment or financial information at any stage of the recruitment process. Project HOPE will never send you a third-party check and ask you to cash it. If you have been recruited via email, please contact Compliance@projecthope.org

Due to the substantial number of inquiries we receive, only applicants who meet the required qualifications and experience for this consultancy will be contacted. No phone calls please. However, since we are active around the world in the field of public health, we may wish to retain your CV in our database for other/future opportunities, unless you direct us otherwise.

Thank you very much for your interest in Project HOPE.

content.rendered:
CULTURE AND ARTS EDITOR – 1

Kantipur Publications is looking for an ambitious and experienced editor to spearhead our coverage of arts & culture. This role will oversee our journalism spanning film, theatre, books, music, visual arts, literature, heritage, content creation, and creative industries—developing stories that examine how culture shapes Nepali society.

The Culture and Arts Editor will commission, edit and produce distinctive coverage across print and

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Lead and shape culture and arts coverage of The Kathmandu Post and Kantipur Daily across print and digital platforms
  • Commission, edit and develop features, profiles, interviews, criticism, reviews and reported stories from in-house and freelance journalists
  • Identify emerging cultural trends, important voices and underreported stories across Nepal
  • Build a strong network of writers, critics, artists, filmmakers, musicians, scholars and cultural practitioners
  •  Collaborate with photo, design, video and digital teams to develop visually compelling storytelling
  •  Maintain high editorial standards for accuracy, fairness, originality and critical independence
  •  Work with the wider editorial team to identify stories that connect culture and the arts to broader social, political and economic questions.

digital platforms, working closely with reporters, critics, freelance contributors, photographers and visual journalists. We are looking for an editor with strong editorial judgment, a deep understanding of Nepal’s cultural scene, and the ability to take the section beyond reviews and event coverage towards ambitious, original journalism. This is a player-coach role – you’ll manage a small team of reporters and are expected to do your own reporting and writing on a regular basis.

CULTURE & ARTS REPORTER – 1

Kantipur Publications is looking for a curious, energetic Culture and Arts Reporter to cover Nepal’s vibrant and evolving cultural scene for Kantipur and The Kathmandu Post. The reporter will cover film, music, books, theatre, visual arts, literature, heritage and creative industries, while developing original stories that go beyond routine event coverage.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR:

  • 1–2 years of journalism experience, preferably in culture and arts
  •  Strong writing and reporting skills in English or Nepali
  •  Genuine interest in Nepal’s cultural and creative landscape
  • Ability to find original stories, interview sources, and report independently

WHO YOU ARE

  • An experienced journalist or editor with at least 7 years of relevant experience, including meaningful experience editing or commissioning culture and arts journalism
  •  A strong writer and editor with excellent command of either English or Nepali language
  •  Deeply familiar with Nepal’s cultural and creative landscape and its major institutions, practitioners, debates and emerging trends
  •  Experienced in commissioning and developing original features, criticism and in-depth cultural journalism
  •  Possesses strong editorial judgment and the ability to distinguish meaningful cultural stories from routine event coverage
  •  Curiosity, initiative, and strong news judgment
  • Experience with multimedia or digital storytelling is an advantage

TO APPLY : By October 15, send:

  • Cover letter
  •  CV/resume
  • Two story ideas you would pursue in your first month
  • Three published work samples

Email: careers@kantipurmediagroup.com

Subject: Culture and Arts Reporter

HOW TO APPLY : To apply, please submit the following by October 15:

  • A cover letter explaining why you want this role and how you would strengthen the culture and arts coverage of Kantipur and The Kathmandu Post
  •  A full CV or resume
  •  Two story ideas you would pursue in your first three months and Three examples of your published work

Send your application to careers@kantipurmediagroup.com with the subject line: Culture and Arts Editor.

The Local Adaptation to Climate Change (LACC) Project supports land use planning and management, integrated water and forest resources management, environmental conservation, climate change adaptation, and disaster risk reduction in Sudurpaschim and Karnali provinces. The Office Secretary plays a crucial role in ensuring efficient office operations by managing administrative tasks, documentation, and logistical support.

The Office Secretary is a long-term support position responsible for providing administrative, secretarial, and logistical assistance to the Project Support Unit (PSU). Key responsibilities include document management, preparation and administration of correspondence, translation between English and Nepali, management of incoming and outgoing letters, organisation of meetings, trainings, seminars, and workshops, and verification of related administrative and hotel documentation.

The position also supports procurement and logistical arrangements and ensures systematic filing, records management, and confidentiality of project information. The role contributes to the efficient day-to-day functioning of the PSU by maintaining organised administrative systems and supporting communication and coordination across project activities. As the majority of project documentation is managed electronically through Microsoft 365 and other digital platforms, fluent IT skills and proficiency in modern office applications are essential requirements for the position. Secretary will need to be able to type Nepali Unicode and have fluent English language skills.

This position offers an opportunity for young professionals to gain experience in office administration within an international development project while contributing to climate resilience efforts in Nepal.

Academic Qualifications: The candidate must have at least an Intermediate (10+2) qualification in Management, Administration, IT, or a related field. Preference will be given to those with a Bachelor’s degree.

Languages: Fluency in written and spoken Nepali and English. Must be able to type Nepali Unicode.

Experience and Skills:

  • Experience in office secretarial work, office management, and/or IT-related tasks, especially in donor-funded or international projects.
  • Candidate should have strong IT skills and proficiency in MS Office (Word, Excel, OneDrive, PowerPoint, Teams, Outlook) and internet use, along with excellent organizational, time management, and multitasking skills.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal abilities, the capacity to work both independently and in a team.
  • A high level of discretion and confidentiality are essential.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Administrative and Secretarial Support
  • Manage official correspondence, reports, and project documentation in both digital and hard-copy formats.
  • Draft letters, templates, routine correspondence, and administrative documents.
  • Translate documents, correspondence, and reports between Nepali and English.
  • Prepare meeting minutes, event reports, and incident reports as required.
  • Maintain filing, registration, archiving, and records management systems for incoming and outgoing correspondence and project documents.
  • Maintain and update the project library, including reports, guidelines, manuals, and reference materials.
  • Monitor staff timesheets and leave records, and follow up on timely submission and filing of supporting documentation.
  • Maintain records of staff leave, holidays, field visits, and field reports in coordination with CAFO.
  • Prepare and maintain framework contract documentation and related administrative records.
  • Provide day-to-day administrative and secretarial support to the CAFO and PSU team.

Logistics and Office Management

  • Arrange travel, accommodation, and logistical support for project staff, consultants, and visitors in coordination with the Operational Manager.
  • Serve as the primary reception and contact point for visitors, guests, and external stakeholders.
  • Provide administrative and logistical support for meetings, trainings, workshops, seminars, and other project events.
  • Coordinate office supplies, consumables, refreshments, drinking water, and other routine office requirements.
  • Maintain and update staff contact lists and internal administrative records.
  • Coordinate the production, issuance, and collection of staff identity cards, visiting cards, and project visibility materials.
  • Support the supervision and coordination of office support personnel, including office assistants, cleaners, and security staff, in coordination with the CAFO.
  • Follow up on operational invoices, vendor documentation, and administrative records related to office operations.
  • Maintain vendor databases, standing lists, and related procurement documentation in accordance with project procedures.

HR and Finance Support

  • Verify supporting documentation related to training events, workshops, seminars, hotel services, participant allowances, and other administrative expenditures before submission for processing.
  • Collect and organise invoices, receipts, attendance records, and supporting documents required for payment processing.
  • Check hotel quotations, venue rates, and service packages, and prepare price comparison documentation for approval.
  • Support the administration of staff medical, accident, vehicle, and asset insurance, including renewals and claims follow-up.
  • Assist in processing insurance claims, reimbursements, and other administrative payments.
  • Maintain records, summaries, and supporting documentation related to office operational expenditures.
  • Recommend properly supported expenditures to the Accountant for processing in accordance with established procedures.

Logistics Related Support

  • Obtain quotations and assess venue suitability, costs, and facilities for trainings, seminars, workshops, and meetings in close coordination with the Operational Manager.
  • Coordinate venue bookings and logistical arrangements, including accommodation, catering, and training packages.
  • Arrange and distribute training materials, stationery, participant certificates, and other event supplies.
  • Coordinate the collection of supplies and materials from the store and ensure timely availability for events.
  • Maintain attendance records and supporting documentation for training and workshop activities.
  • Provide on-site logistical support to ensure the smooth implementation of trainings, seminars, workshops, and meetings.

Other Responsibilities

  • Undertake additional tasks assigned by the management and project administration team to support project goals.
  • Maintain confidentiality in all aspects of work.

Any other tasks assigned by the Supervisor

title.rendered: Field Coordinator, Monitoring and Evaluation Coordinator, Childcare Space Facilitator,  Procurement Officer, Coordinator – Mental Health and Psychosocial Support

content.rendered:
SOS Children’s Villages Nepal, a non-governmental social development organisation, supports children without parental care and families in difficult living conditions through services in care, education, health and emergency relief. We advocate for the rights of children and young people, in alliance with a great diversity of partners. We offer a secure and friendly work environment and are committed to safeguarding the rights of children by having zero tolerance policy in this regard. We are further committed to providing a safe environment for coworkers and children, young people and adults with whom we work, where human rights are respected and upheld, and healthy relations are fostered by building organisational systems, capacity, and awareness on our Child and Youth Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct. We are now looking for interested and qualified individuals for various full- time contract positions under the Nepal Multi-location Flood Response Project.

Job positions:

1. Field Coordinator: 3 (Based in Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading – one position in each location)

The Field Coordinator, under the supervision of the Emergency Response Manager, plays a pivotal role in coordinating and overseeing the effective implementation of the emergency response and recovery programme at the field level. The position requires strong organisational, leadership, coordination and interpersonal skills, along with a good understanding of the programme’s key areas, including child and youth safeguarding, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), education, WASH, basic needs, livelihood recovery and disaster risk reduction. This role involves working closely with local government authorities, communities, schools, service providers and other stakeholders to ensure timely, quality and effective delivery of programme interventions, while requiring the ability to respond to emerging needs, address implementation challenges, and provide practical solutions in dynamic field situations.

Key performance areas and main responsibilities:

  • Collaborate with the Emergency Response Manager and relevant stakeholders to develop, coordinate and implement the programme plan in line with project objectives and agreed timelines.
  • Lead and support programme planning and implementation at the municipality and community level, covering child and youth safeguarding, MHPSS, childcare spaces (CCS), education, WASH, basic needs, livelihoods and disaster risk reduction interventions.
  • Establish and maintain effective coordination with local government authorities, community leaders, schools, service providers, contractors and other relevant stakeholders to ensure smooth and timely programme implementation.
  •  Coordinate and supervise field teams, provide necessary technical and operational guidance, and identify capacity-building needs to ensure quality and effective delivery of programme activities.
  •  Oversee field-level resource planning, budget utilisation, activity monitoring and documentation; ensure appropriate beneficiary identification, service delivery, referral and community engagement in accordance with programme standards and organisational policies.
  • Monitor programme progress, identify implementation gaps and risks, and prepare timely and comprehensive progress reports and updates for submission to the relevant management.

Qualifications, experience and skills:

  •  A minimum of a Master’s degree in a relevant field (e.g., Development Studies, Social Sciences, Public Health, Education, Disaster Management, Rural Development, Management, Livelihoods, etc.), with at least a second division or equivalent from a recognised university.
  •  A minimum of three years’ experience in programme/project management and field-level coordination, preferably in humanitarian response, emergency recovery, child protection, education, community development, WASH, livelihoods, health, nutrition or disaster risk reduction.
  • Demonstrated experience in coordinating with local government, government agencies, communities and other stakeholders, with a proven track record in programme implementation, partnership building and community engagement.
  •  Knowledge and understanding of child and youth safeguarding, MHPSS, gender and disability inclusion, humanitarian principles and disaster risk reduction will be an advantage.
  •  Experience in coordinating rehabilitation, renovation or construction-related activities and monitoring field-level infrastructure works will be an advantage.
  •  Strong communication skills in English and Nepali, with proficiency in computer applications, including report writing.
  •  Excellent planning, coordination, leadership and problem-solving skills, with a positive attitude and willingness to work and travel in challenging field conditions.

2. Monitoring and Evaluation Coordinator: 1

The Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Coordinator, under the supervision of the Emergency Response Manager, plays a vital role in ensuring effective monitoring, documentation, and reporting of the emergency response and recovery programme. The position is responsible for establishing and maintaining appropriate Monitoring and Evaluation systems, tracking programme progress and results, ensuring data quality, and generating evidence to support programme learning, accountability, and informed decision-making.

Key performance areas and main responsibilities:

  • Develop and implement a comprehensive Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) framework aligned with programme objectives, indicators, targets, and reporting requirements, including appropriate data collection tools and methodologies.
  • Establish and maintain effective systems for regular collection, compilation, compilation, verification, storage, and analysis of quantitative and qualitative programme data from field locations and different programme components.
  • Monitor programme indicators and targets across key intervention areas, including child and youth safeguarding, MHPSS, childcare space (CCS), education, WASH, basic needs, livelihoods, and disaster risk reduction, and track progress against the approved programme plan.
  •  Conduct regular field monitoring and data verification visits to assess the quality, relevance, timeliness and effectiveness of programme activities and provide recommendations for improvement.
  •  Facilitate orientation and provide guidance to field staff and relevant coworkers on data collection tools, M&E processes, data quality, documentation, and reporting requirements.
  •  Prepare periodic M&E updates and progress reports, consolidate programme results and key findings, and provide timely analysis and evidence to support programme reporting, learning, and decision-making.
  • Support the documentation of lessons learned, good practices, challenges, beneficiary feedback, and programme outcomes, and ensure that findings are communicated to relevant programme teams and management.

Qualifications, experience and skills:

  • A minimum of a Master’s degree in a relevant field (e.g., Development Studies, Social Sciences, Public Health, Education, Economics, Statistics, Development Management, or other relevant disciplines), with at least a second division or equivalent from a recognised university.
  •  A minimum of three years’ relevant experience in monitoring and evaluation, preferably in humanitarian response, emergency recovery, development or community-based programmes.
  •  Demonstrated experience in developing M&E frameworks, indicators, data collection tools, data analysis, field monitoring, data quality assurance, and programme reporting.
  •  Experience in working with digital data collection and analysis tools and proficiency in computer applications, particularly MS Excel and other relevant data management or reporting tools.
  •  Strong analytical, communication and report-writing skills in English and Nepali, with the ability to present findings and translate data into practical recommendations.
  • Strong coordination and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with field teams, programme staff, local stakeholders and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Strong attention to detail, commitment to data quality and integrity, and a positive attitude with willingness to travel to programme locations and undertake field monitoring visits.

3. Coordinator – Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS): 1

The Coordinator – MHPSS, under the supervision of the Emergency Response Manager, will be responsible for planning, implementing, coordinating and monitoring psychosocial support and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) activities for children, young people, caregivers and other vulnerable individuals affected by the floods and related emergencies. The position will work closely with field teams, communities, local authorities and health and protection service providers to ensure appropriate psychosocial support, counselling, referral and mental health awareness services.

Key performance areas and main responsibilities:

  •  Provide Psychological First Aid (PFA), structured MHPSS activities and counselling services to affected children, caregivers and vulnerable individuals.
  • Conduct psychosocial needs assessments and identify vulnerable individuals and groups requiring appropriate support and referral.
  •  Plan and implement psychosocial support activities in affected communities, Child-Friendly Spaces and other programme locations.
  • Strengthen referral pathways and coordinate with local governments, health facilities, protection actors and other relevant service providers to facilitate access to specialised services.
  • Support child protection and safeguarding activities, including community awareness on child protection, prevention of Gender-Based Violence (GBV), and available support services.
  •  Monitor psychosocial activities, document progress and challenges, and provide regular updates and reports to the relevant programme team.

Qualifications, experience and skills:

  • A minimum of a Master’s degree in Psychology with at least three years of relevant work experience; or a Master’s degree in any discipline with a one-year Postgraduate Diploma in Psychological Counselling and at least three years of relevant work experience.
  •  Experience in psychosocial support, MHPSS, counselling, social work, protection, or humanitarian programming, preferably with experience working with children, caregivers, and communities affected by emergencies or displacement.
  •  Experience in working with communities affected by disasters, displacement or other emergencies will be an added advantage.
  •  Strong communication skills in both English and Nepali, along with proficiency in computer applications.
  •  Strong interpersonal, coordination and facilitation skills, with a positive attitude.

4. Procurement Officer: 1

The Procurement Officer, under the supervision of the Emergency Response Manager, is responsible for planning, coordinating, and managing procurement activities for the emergency response and recovery programme. The position will work closely with programme and field teams to ensure the timely, cost-effective, transparent, and compliant procurement and delivery of required goods, works, and services in line with organisational procurement policies and applicable laws.

Key performance areas and main responsibilities:

  • Coordinate procurement planning and processes with programme and field teams to ensure timely availability of required goods, works, and services.
  •  Obtain and evaluate quotations, coordinate with suppliers and service providers, and facilitate procurement in line with organisational policies, donor requirements, and applicable procedures.
  • Coordinate the procurement and delivery of programme and emergency response items, including shelter materials, WASH supplies, educational materials, and other required goods and services.
  • Follow up with suppliers and service providers to ensure timely delivery and address procurement-related issues in coordination with relevant teams.
  • Maintain complete and accurate procurement records, monitor procurement expenditure against approved budgets, and provide timely updates on procurement progress, challenges, and pending requirements.

Qualifications, experience and skills:

  • A minimum of Bachelor degree in Business Administration, Business Studies or relevant degree with at least a second division or its equivalent from a recognised university.
  • At least three years of relevant experience in procurement, supply chain, or logistics, preferably with an NGO or development organisation.
  •  Experience in procurement processes, vendor management, documentation, and compliance with organisational requirements, including procurement of emergency response items, WASH supplies, shelter materials, and educational materials.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, coordination, and computer skills, with proficiency in English and Nepali.
  • Strong interpersonal and organisational skills, with a positive attitude.

5. Childcare Space Facilitator: 3 (Based in Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading – one position in each location)

The Childcare Space Facilitator, under the supervision of the Field Coodinator, is responsible for supporting the day-to-day operation of safe, inclusive and supportive spaces for children affected by the crisis. The position will facilitate age-appropriate learning, recreational and psychosocial activities and work closely with children, caregivers, volunteers and community members to promote children’s well-being and protection.

Key performance areas and main responsibilities:

  • Facilitate age-appropriate educational, recreational, life skills and psychosocial activities for children at Child-Friendly Spaces.
  •  Ensure a safe, inclusive and child-friendly environment and promote the safety, protection and well-being of children attending space.
  •  Identify children who may require additional support and refer concerns to the appropriate programme staff through established referral pathways.
  •  Communicate and build positive relationships with children, caregivers and community members and encourage their participation in CFS activities.
  •  Coordinate with the Field Coordinator, Psychosocial Coordinator, schools and community stakeholders for effective implementation of activities.
  •  Maintain basic records of activities and attendance and submit regular updates to the Field Coordinator.

Qualifications, experience and skills:

  •  A minimum of a High School Graduate (10+2) qualification with at least a second division or equivalent.
  •  Preference will be given to candidates with at least one year of experience working with children, families or community-based programmes.
  • Strong communication skills in both English and Nepali, along with proficiency in computer applications.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and a positive attitude.

Salary and other benefits: As per the policies of the organisation.

Interested candidates are requested to apply with a Cover Letter, Curriculum Vitae, Copies of Academic Certificates, (equivalence from relevant government agencies if studied out of Nepal), Copy of Citizenship Certificate, a passport size photo and the Employment Application Form (mandatory document to be downloaded from here) to: vacancy@sosnepal.org.np by 5: 00 pm, October 9, 2026.

SOS Children’s Villages Nepal reserves the right to reject any or all the applications without assigning any reason whatsoever. SOS Children’s Villages Nepal follows the Inclusive Policy and therefore encourages women, people with disabilities, people of ethnic minorities and marginalised communities to apply.

FAO’s commitment to environmental sustainability is integral to our strategic objectives and operations.

Organizational Setting

FAO is a specialized agency of the UN that leads international efforts to defeat hunger. FAO’s goal is to achieve food security for all and ensure that people have regular access to enough high-quality food to lead active, healthy lives. With 195 Members (194 countries and the European Union), FAO works in over 130 countries worldwide.

FAO Country Offices, working under overall corporate guidance and in line with the Strategic Framework, offer policy advice and support to countries in the mandated areas of FAO, facilitated through partnerships, resources and an active country programme to provide technical assistance, develop capacities and deliver core services while fully observing international standards of accountability to establish leadership and strengthen impact at the country level.

The offices deliver on the programmatic priorities of each country as agreed in their respective Country Programming Frameworks (CPFs) aligned to the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) and ensure effective and efficient operations with adequate human and financial resources.

Specifically, FAO Country Offices:

  • advocate, inform and support policies and investments in the areas of FAO’s mandate;
  • provide technical assistance and deliver core services;
  • assist and catalyse partnership and resource mobilization activities to support agrifood systems transformation;
  • Position FAO as the specialized/authoritative technical agency in food and agriculture and agrifood systems transformation;
  • ensure risk-smart and accountable operations and management.

The position is located in the Sudurpashchim Province, based in the Provincial office of the FAO Nepal Country Office, and will support the field implementation of projects in the region. The Provincial Coordinator for Sudurpaschim Province will serve as the primary focal point for the project at the provincial level, ensuring effective planning, coordination, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of project activities in close collaboration with provincial and local government authorities, implementing partners, community stakeholders, and FAO Nepal. The incumbent will facilitate stakeholder engagement, strengthen partnerships, support work plan development and execution, monitor progress against agreed targets, identify and address implementation bottlenecks, ensure compliance with project requirements and donor obligations, organize meetings and capacity development activities, and contribute to knowledge management, documentation, and reporting. The Provincial Coordinator will also provide strategic and technical support to promote alignment of project interventions with provincial priorities, enhance local ownership, and ensure the timely achievement of project outcomes and sustainable impact across Sudurpaschim Province.

Reporting Lines

The Provincial Coordinator works under the overall supervision of the FAOR in Nepal, direct supervision of the Assistant FAOR (Programme), and in close coordination with the Emergency and Resilience Coordinator, and the technical supervision of the FAORAP/HQs, and in close consultation and coordination with the government counterparts.

Technical Focus

The Provincial Coordinator will support provincial-level planning, coordination, implementation, monitoring and reporting of FAO projects in Sudurpashchim Province and the western region of Lumbini Province, with emphasis on stakeholder coordination, capacity development, quality assurance, climate resilience, gender equality and social inclusion, and timely achievement of project results.

Tasks and responsibilities

  • Coordinate provincial-level planning and implementation of ReFAME activities in line with the project document and approved annual work plans, ensuring disaggregated planning by year, district, and budget headings.
  • Support the Project Management Unit (PMU) in effective execution of project activities, including finalization of Letters of Agreement (LOA)/contracts in consultation with the PMU, and maintain close coordination with the FAO Nepal Country Office.
  •  Conduct regular field monitoring visits to track progress, address implementation bottlenecks, and ensure quality and timely delivery.
  • Coordinate and maintain strong working relationships with the PMU, Ministry of Industry, Tourism, Forest and Environment (Sudurpashchim Province), Division Forest Offices, Provincial Ministries, Local Governments, UN agencies, INGOs, NGOs, and other relevant stakeholders to ensure harmonized, complementary, and sustainable interventions.
  •  Lead and support capacity-building initiatives, including capacitating human resources hired by the Operational Partner (OP), government counterparts, community institutions, and project beneficiaries for smooth implementation.
  •  Develop concept notes and detailed budget estimates for project activities and events, integrating gender equality, social inclusion, and climate resilience considerations.
  •  Support and monitor implementation of related FAO projects in Sudurpashchim and western region of Lumbini Province (e.g., ReFAME, GAFSP-PO, Four Better Model Village) to ensure quality of implementation, synergy and complementarities.
  • Facilitate visits from FAO CO, RAP, HQ, government counterparts, and other stakeholders, and coordinate with technical officers for necessary support.
  •  Represent FAO Nepal at provincial and local coordination meetings, workshops, and technical forums, including emergency-response, food security and nutrition coordination mechanisms and line agencies.
  •  Apply accountability and quality assurance mechanisms, organize periodic review and reflection meetings, coordinate Project Task Force meetings, and prepare required progress reports (quarterly, biannual, annual) in line with project, OPA, and donor requirements, documenting lessons learned and good practices.
  •  Provide coordination support to short-term consultants and undertake additional technical, coordination, or operational assignments (e.g., ITB, RFQ, RFP, BOQ, M&E, reporting, proposal development, etc.) as requested by the FAO Country Office to ensure effective achievement of project results.

CANDIDATES WILL BE ASSESSED AGAINST THE FOLLOWING

Minimum Requirements

  • Master’s degree in agricultural science, international development, natural resource management, climate change or any other related field.
  • At least five years of progressive professional experience in implementation, coordination and management of agriculture, agrifood systems, rural development, climate resilience, natural resource management or development programmes.
  •  Working knowledge of English (level C).
  •  National of Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal or resident of the country with a valid work permit.

FAO Core Competencies

  •  Results Focus
  • Teamwork
  • Communication
  • Building Effective Relationships
  •  Knowledge Sharing and Continuous Improvement

Technical/Functional Skills

  •  Work experience in more than one location or area of work, particularly in field-based assignments.
  • Extent and relevance of experience in coordinating agriculture, agrifood systems, rural development, climate resilience or natural resource management projects.
  •  Demonstrated experience working with provincial and local governments, civil society organizations, UN agencies, development partners and other stakeholders.
  •  Experience in project planning, monitoring, reporting, budgeting, capacity development and coordination of service providers or operational partners.

Selection Criteria

  •  Strong experience in provincial-level coordination, field implementation and stakeholder engagement.
  • Proven ability to prepare and monitor work plans, budgets, procurement-related inputs, risk registers and progress reports.
  •  Demonstrated capacity to organize and facilitate training, workshops, review meetings and technical coordination forums.
  • Strong skills in monitoring implementation, documenting results, preparing reports and addressing operational bottlenecks.
  •  Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work collaboratively and deliver results under pressure

The National Federation of the Disabled Nepal (NFDN) is a national umbrella organization of persons with disabilities and has been consistently working to promote and protect the rights of persons with disabilities in Nepal since 1993. NFDN is seeking a highly qualified, experienced and motivated professionals for the position of Project Coordinator to implement Include Us phase II project supported by CBM Global Nepal.

Interested candidates are requested to visit the NFDN website, www.nfdn.org.np review the detailed Terms of Reference/Job Description and required qualifications and submit their application along with the following documents:

  •  An updated CV;
  •  A cover letter mentioning the expected salary; and
  •  Contact details, including telephone number and email address of two referees.

The interested candidates are requested to apply from the online link: https://ee.kobotoolbox.org/x/QcKDFIvF no later than October 17, 2026.

NFDN reserves the right to cancel, postpone, modify or withdraw the recruitment process, and to reject any application without assigning any reason.

Candidates applying for these positions must comply with NFDN’s policies, guidelines, and code of conduct, including its Safeguarding, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH), and Anti-Corruption policies, as well as all associated standards and procedures.

1. Project Coordinator- NFDN Federal Office Kathmandu

Job purpose:

The Project Coordinator (PC) is responsible for overseeing the overall project cycle management of the Include Us Phase II Project and related NFDN programmes, ensuring effective, timely, inclusive and quality implementation in line with NFDN’s principles, policies, strategic priorities and agreed project standards. The PC will provide technical and strategic support to project and provincial staff, coordinate with OPDs, government authorities, partners, donors and other stakeholders and oversee programme planning, advocacy, capacity building, awareness raising, networking, budget management, communication, reporting, monitoring and evaluation. The PC will serve as NFDN’s focal point for federal and provincial project coordination, promote the meaningful participation of persons with all types of disabilities, support project and resource development and ensure that good practices, evidence and lessons learned are documented and applied to strengthen NFDN’s programmes.

Major Responsibilities

1. Project Planning, Implementation and Quality Assurance

  • Lead the planning, implementation, monitoring and quality assurance of project activities in accordance with the approved project design, agreement, workplan, budget, indicators, NFDN strategy and roadmap.
  •  Develop appropriate implementation modalities, processes, tools and workplans and ensure that activities are implemented effectively, on time and within the approved budget.
  • Ensure timely planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, review and reporting of project activities, with appropriate quality assurance throughout the project cycle.
  •  Ensure that project approaches and interventions are responsive to the needs and priorities of persons with disabilities and comply with NFDN, partner and donor policies, procedures and standards.
  •  Monitor project progress against agreed outputs, results, deliverables and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), and take or recommend corrective measures where necessary.
  •  Contribute to the achievement of monthly and quarterly project operational and quality targets.
  •  Ensure meaningful participation of persons with disabilities and OPDs representing different impairment groups in project planning, implementation, monitoring and review.

2. Provincial and Local-Level Coordination

  • Monitor the implementation of project activities by provincial offices and provide technical guidance, mentoring, recommendations and corrective support to Province Managers, Province Advocacy Officers and other relevant staff.
  • Provide technical support and guidance for project activities at provincial, district and municipal levels.
  •  Coordinate with OPDs in project-targeted provinces and municipalities to facilitate their meaningful engagement in advocacy, policy dialogue, access to justice, accessibility and other project initiatives.
  •  Coordinate with federal, provincial and local government authorities, OPDs, rights holders, civil society organizations and other relevant stakeholders to facilitate effective project implementation.
  • Explore and strengthen networking and collaboration opportunities at federal, provincial and local levels relevant to the project.

3. Advocacy, Disability Rights and Capacity Building

  • Promote and support a human rights-based and disability-inclusive approach in all project activities, consistent with the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD), national legislation and relevant international standards.
  • Support OPDs and persons with disabilities to advocate for their rights, access to justice, accessibility and inclusive policies and programmes.
  • Contribute to the development of advocacy strategies for consideration by the NFDN Board to influence relevant federal, provincial and local authorities in strengthening disability-inclusive policies, programmes and services.
  •  Identify capacity-building needs and facilitate training, orientation, coaching and mentoring for project staff, OPDs, persons with disabilities and other relevant stakeholders in coordination with the Administrative Manager and General Secretary.
  • Support NFDN Board members in project-related advocacy campaigns, awareness-raising, capacity-building, networking and collaboration activities.

4. Monitoring, Evaluation, Reporting and Learning

  • Develop and maintain appropriate tools and formats for collecting, analysing and documenting project data from national, provincial, district, municipal and OPD levels.
  •  Ensure systematic monitoring of project progress, results, achievements, challenges, lessons learned and good practices.
  •  Conduct or facilitate quarterly internal reviews covering programme, operational and financial performance, and provide constructive feedback and recommendations for improvement.
  • Prepare monthly, periodic narrative and other reports required by NFDN, project partners and donors in accordance with agreed reporting requirements.
  • Ensure that reports accurately capture relevant data, progress, results, achievements, challenges, case studies, lessons learned and good practices.
  • Prepare and document case studies, success stories and other evidence of project results and impact.
  • Ensure that project information, relevant national and international legal frameworks, policies, guidelines, research and other useful resources are compiled and shared with NFDN member organizations through accessible communication channels, including email, telephone, website, social media, publications, meetings and orientations.

5. Coordination, Communication and Project Governance

  • Facilitate effective communication and coordination among the project team, NFDN management, Board members, provincial offices, OPDs, partners and other stakeholders.
  • Ensure that project staff, Board members and key stakeholders have a clear understanding of project objectives, expected results, roles and responsibilities, and provide leadership and motivation to achieve agreed goals.
  • Organize and facilitate meetings of project partners, the Project Steering Committee and other project structures in accordance with the approved implementation plan.
  • Prepare agendas, minutes, action points and other necessary documentation and ensure timely follow-up on agreed decisions.
  • Provide regular and timely information to the Administrative Manager and General Secretary on project progress, implementation issues, risks, opportunities, financial and operational matters, and required management decisions.
  • Liaise, in coordination with the Line Manager, with the International Office, I/NGOs, project partners, consultants, advisors, NFDN Board members, Province Managers and other stakeholders connected with the project.

6. Risk Management and Technical Quality

  •  Ensure that appropriate technical quality standards are maintained throughout project implementation.
  •  Identify, document and analyse technical, operational and implementation risks and opportunities and recommend appropriate mitigation or improvement measures.
  •  Collect and analyse relevant technical information and ensure that evidence and lessons learned inform project planning and implementation.
  •  Ensure compliance with NFDN, partner and donor requirements and established project procedures.

7. Project Development and Resource Mobilization

  •  Identify emerging needs, opportunities and innovative approaches for the development of new projects and programmes aligned with NFDN’s strategic priorities.
  •  Support the Administrative Manager and General Secretary in donor mapping, resource mobilization, proposal development and submission to potential partners and donors.
  •  Develop concise concept notes or one-page activity papers for planned activities based on the approved project plan before implementation and facilitate the required internal approval process.
  • Document and promote innovative practices, lessons learned and evidence that can contribute to future programme development.

8. Overall Accountability

  •  Ensure that project activities are implemented efficiently, effectively and transparently, with appropriate accountability for time, budget, quality and results.
  •  Perform other project-related duties and responsibilities assigned by the General Secretary, Administrative Manager or other authorized NFDN authority in accordance with NFDN policies and procedures.
  • Regular implementation and follow up of the programs and also follow the recommendations arising from the reviews, audits, monitoring visits and internal and donor assessment
  • Be responsible for ensuring the expenditure follows approved budgets, approvals, donor and organisational policies, documentation requirements.

Qualification, experiences and skills requirements:

  • Master degree in social work, development studies, education, management, law or related field (disability study is preferred).
  • Minimum of five years of experience in I/NGO environment, including experience coordinating and implementing programs. besides project management experience, specifically require demonstrated experience with the donor compliance, budget monitoring, internal controls and procurement procedures.
  •  Experience in social sector with a proven experience of working with persons with disabilities/OPD. (Experience on disability inclusion related project or advocacy is preferred).
  •  Good skills of the risk identification and prompt response to the risks as stated in the risk register
  •  Good knowledge and understanding of UNCRPD and national law related to disability.
  •  Good understanding of disability context / concerns and rights
  •  Good experience in disability inclusion and accessibility with leadership quality to coordinate and influence the governments bodies.
  •  Good experience of working with different impairment groups/OPDs at province & municipal level.
  •  Strong communication, documentation, coordination and team-building skills.
  •  Excellent written and verbal communication in Nepali and English
  •  Good computer skill in operating basic computer programs such as MS office packs with email and internet handling
  • Skillful in searching information in internet, operating social media, making news, activity, and periodic reports when needed.

    NFDN follows the organization policies and guidelines including safeguarding and anti-corruption policies and ensure compliance to all aspects of the Safeguarding and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, abuse and harassment policies and associated standards and procedures. NFDN is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified women and person with disability are strongly encouraged to apply. NFDN always encourage the inclusion and integration of people with disabilities and female candidate in its program and plans.

Organizational Setting

FAO is a specialized agency of the UN that leads international efforts to defeat hunger. FAO’s goal is to achieve food security for all and ensure that people have regular access to enough high-quality food to lead active, healthy lives. With 195 Members (194 countries and the European Union), FAO works in over 130 countries worldwide.

FAO Country Offices, working under overall corporate guidance and in line with the Strategic Framework, offer policy advice and support to countries in the mandated areas of FAO, facilitated through partnerships, resources and an active country programme to provide technical assistance, develop capacities and deliver core services while fully observing international standards of accountability to establish leadership and strengthen impact at the country level.

The offices deliver on the programmatic priorities of each country as agreed in their respective Country Programming Frameworks (CPFs) aligned to the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) and ensure effective and efficient operations with adequate human and financial resources.

Specifically, FAO Country Offices:

  • advocate, inform and support policies and investments in the areas of FAO’s mandate;
  • provide technical assistance and deliver core services;
  •  assist and catalyse partnership and resource mobilization activities to support agrifood systems transformation;
  •  Position FAO as the specialized/authoritative technical agency in food and agriculture and agrifood systems transformation;
  •  ensure risk-smart and accountable operations and management.

Reporting Lines

The Programme Assistant will work under the overall supervision of the FAO Representative and direct supervision of the Assistant FAO Representative (Programme) in close consultation with programme cluster team.

Technical Focus

The Programme Assistant provides technical and operational support for project implementation by preparing programme documents and reports, compiling and analysing data from corporate systems, and ensuring accurate documentation and filing. The role supports monitoring activities, organizes meetings and missions, manages correspondence, and assists in producing background materials. It also contributes to project coordination, logistical arrangements, and routine administrative tasks to ensure smooth delivery of programme operations.

Tasks and responsibilities

  • Assist in the preparation of project proposals/documents, project briefs, project progress/final reports, background papers, sections of reports and studies.

  •  Process, format and proof-read reports, documents, publications, and correspondence related to the work of the Country office from draft texts.
  •  Review and direct correspondence, calls and queries to appropriate contacts; provide for background information; respond to routine enquiries.
  •  Assist in the organization of policy dialogues, workshops and consultation meetings and preparation for project periodic reviews, field monitoring and supervision missions in close consultation with programme team, government counterparts and other relevant stakeholders.
  •  Make arrangements for meetings, seminars and events: implement logistics, prepare meeting minutes, correspondences, compile and distribute documents, support in administrative arrangements.
  •  Enter, select, analyse, and summarize data from various sources, including FAO corporate systems, such as COIN (Country Office Information System), FPMIS (Field Programme Management Information System), Global Resource Management System (GRMS), country databases, etc to support programme operations.
  •  Maintain log, file and update records in prescribed format for subsequent use.
  •  Participate in project monitoring by maintaining current registers and controlling tools on the status of projects at various stages; review inputs, expenditures, and time frames according to work plans; make necessary abstracts and computations; detect inconsistencies.
  •  Assist in the preparation and submission of periodic and ad hoc project and country office reports.
  •  Prepare background material, working papers and tables for briefings, review sessions and meetings.
  •  Prepare correspondence to verify data, answer queries, and obtain additional information on transactions and operational matters, as required.
  •  Maintain a filing system of technical and project documents and correspondence.
  •  Carry out other specific operational tasks for programme/ project implementation as requested.
  • Perform other related duties as required.

TPO Nepal is implementing a project named “Mental Health and Psycho-social Support interventions to Individuals, Families and Communities affected by the Flash Flood” funded by Americares Foundation, which aims to improve the mental health, psychosocial well-being, functioning and resilience of individuals, families and communities affected by the flash flood through evidence based MHPSS interventions and strengthened community and health system support.

NIDWAN is a national non-profit organization led by Indigenous women with disabilities, working to promote dignity, equality, and social justice for Indigenous women and girls with disabilities across Nepal. NIDWAN’s vision is a just, inclusive, and equitable society where Indigenous women including underrepresented groups with disabilities, fully enjoy their human rights and actively participate in all spheres of life. Its mission is to empower Indigenous and underrepresented groups with disabilities through advocacy, leadership development, access to inclusive services (including health and SRH), and strengthened institutional and community systems that uphold their rights. NIDWAN is guided by core values and principles of human rights, gender equality, disability inclusion, Indigenous peoples’ rights, participation and leadership of persons with disabilities with an intersectional approach, accountability, and partnership. NIDWAN has been working collaboratively with Government, UN agencies like WFP, UNDP, UN Women, civil society, and development partners to ensure that no one is left behind. In addition, NIDWAN has done movement building with feminist, disability, indigenous and youth movements. From its decade-long experiences, NIDWAN is equipped with competencies regarding gender-responsive and disability inclusive education, climate, health care systems, and health-related social services.

Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

Employee Contract Type: Local – Fixed Term Employee (Fixed Term)

Job Description:

This position is responsible for performing financial accounting, account reconciliation, and review of expenses, including the processing and review of journal entries and vouchers in the financial system. The position will also support the preparation of accounting records and financial statements and oversee accounts payable and receivable activities in compliance with WVI financial policies, standards, and applicable statutory requirements.

The position will be responsible for ensuring the effective and efficient utilization and management of organizational financial resources through strong financial controls, timely and accurate reporting, compliance, and continuous improvement of financial systems and processes, ultimately contributing to better stewardship of resources for the benefit of children and communities.

In addition, the position will oversee the overall financial management, compliance, reporting, and control requirements related to US Government-funded activities and the Flood Response Project, ensuring adherence to applicable donor regulations, WVI policies and procedures, grant requirements, and statutory obligations. The position will coordinate closely with relevant Finance, Programme, Operations, and partner teams to ensure proper financial planning, monitoring, documentation, and accountability throughout the project lifecycle.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Financial Management and Multi-Donor Response Funding administration

  • Manage financial operations of Response Funding in accordance with diverse donor regulations, organizational policies, and approved budgets.
  • Maintain clear segment accounting to track, allocate, and monitor contributions coming from different funding organizations, ensuring no co-mingling of restricted funds.
  • Monitor project expenditures across all funding streams to ensure costs are allowable, allocable, reasonable, and properly documented according to specific donor agreements.
  • Review transactions and supporting documents for compliance with various donor requirements and organizational guidelines.
  • Monitor budget utilization across multiple donor accounts and provide regular analysis on spending trends, burn rates, and potential funding gaps.
  • Support project teams in multi-donor budget planning, budget revisions, co-funding allocations, and financial forecasting.
  • Ensure sufficient fund availability and proper donor account coding prior to processing response-related payments.

Financial Reporting

  • Prepare accurate and timely monthly, quarterly, annual, and donor-specific financial reports for management, institutional grants, and other funding sources in compliance with donor and Support Office (SO) templates.
  • Review General Ledger transactions to ensure proper expense coding and allocation across multiple funding streams.
  • Conduct regular account reconciliations, including bank accounts, advances, receivables, grant balances, cash receipts, and commitments against SO agreements.
  • Track matched funding and co-financing requirements between institutional grants and complementary funding sources.
  • Prepare financial analyses, variance reports, and pipeline updates for project management, grant closeout activities, and donor/SO review meetings.
  • Consolidate multi-donor financial data and resolve reporting queries from Support Offices, National Offices, and donor representatives.

Compliance and Internal Controls

  • Ensure compliance with terms, conditions, and regulations governing all contributing donor organizations, as well as organizational policies.
  • Maintain adequate supporting documentation, donor mapping records, and grant files for internal and external audit purposes.
  • Conduct periodic financial compliance reviews to manage risks associated with multi-donor funding rules and restrictions.
  • Support internal audits, external audits, donor-specific audits, and monitoring visits from funding partners.
  • Implement corrective action plans for audit findings and donor compliance recommendations.

Partner Financial Monitoring

  • Review partner financial reports, supporting documents, and fund utilization to ensure accuracy, completeness, and compliance.
  • Conduct periodic financial monitoring visits and desk reviews of implementing partners.

The incumbent will work closely together with World Vision and partner NGO staff, as well as with the education department government staff. Transcultural Psychosocial Organization Nepal (TPO) Nepal is one of Nepal’s leading psychosocial organizations. It was established in 2005 to promote psychosocial well-being and mental health of people in conflict-affected and other vulnerable communities through the development of sustainable, culturally-appropriate, and community-based psychosocial support systems.

Project information:

TPO Nepal is implementing activities under the “Strengthen systems for prevention and promotion of child and adolescent mental health” Flood Response project. The project aims to delivery safe, inclusive, ethical and quality mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) to children, adolescents, caregivers, families and other affected and vulnerable populations in communities affected by Bhotekoshi-Rasuwa Flash flood.

For this purpose, TPO Nepal seeks competent, committed and result oriented candidates for the following position:

Job Title : Psychiatrist/ MD

Job Station : Nuwakot

Number of Openings : 1 Full time

Job Duration : 6 Months (possibility to extension)

Start Date : At the earliest

Major responsibilities

The MD Psychiatrist will provide specialized clinical and technical leadership to the Community Mental Health Unit (CMHU) in flood-affected districts of Baghmati Province, Nepal, focusing on recovery and continuity of mental health services. The Psychiatrist will be responsible for following duties but not limited to:

  • Support the establishment and functioning of the CMHU and provide clinical supervision to the multidisciplinary team.
  • Conduct outreach clinics, providing psychiatric assessment, consultation, medication, follow-up and timely referral of complex and high-risk cases.
  • Maintain confidential clinical records and prepare required service and programme reports.Coordinate and support to psychologists, psychiatric nurses, counsellors and frontline health workers on case management and referral.
  • Facilitate mental health and psychosocial training, stress management, self-care sessions for frontline health workers.
  • Coordinate with municipalities, health facilities, government authorities and other stakeholders to strengthen community mental health services and referral mechanisms.
  • Ensure safeguarding, confidentiality, informed consent and child-friendly approaches in all service delivery.
  • Perform other relevant mental health services assigned by the organization.

Qualification, Skills and Experience:

  • MD in Psychiatry from a recognized university/institution.Valid registration with the Nepal Medical Council.
  • Relevant experience in providing psychiatric consultation, diagnosis, treatment, and referral services will be an advantage.
  • Experience in conducting mental health camps or providing mental health services in community settings will be preferred.
  • Good communication, interpersonal, documentation, and coordination skills.
  • Willingness to work in field settings and travel within the assigned area as required.
  • Commitment to confidentiality, professional ethics, safeguarding and respectful service delivery.

The National Association of People Living with HIV in Nepal (NAP+N) is a national network established in 2003 and led by people living with HIV (PLHIV). It works in partnership with community-based organizations and local networks across Nepal to address the challenges of HIV and AIDS. NAP+N aims to strengthen community systems, ensure access to healthcare, and uphold the rights and dignity of PLHIV and key populations through advocacy, prevention, care, and support.

NAP+N is implementing the Community-Led Monitoring (CLM) initiative in 10 districts: Jhapa, Sunsari, Parsa, Dhanusha, Kathmandu, Chitwan, Kaski, Rupandehi, Kapilbastu and Kailali. This project aims to empower communities to monitor, evaluate, and improve HIV services through data-driven advocacy.
