Organizational Context

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability. IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe. The IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. The IFRC is currently present in Nepal through a Country Delegation (CD – first established in 1965 with a presence through regional representation at times), providing support to Nepal Red Cross Society (NRCS) programmes and National Society development (NSD) amongst as well as emergency response, other areas. The longer-term mission of the Nepal Delegation is to facilitate organisational growth, technical capacities, partnerships, and resource mobilisation that enable Nepal Red Cross Society to deliver on its humanitarian mandate in the country through the provision of technical support, advocacy, representation and coordination functions, in accordance with Strategy 2030, the IFRC Renewal and annual Operational Plans. The Country Delegation also provides integration services to six IFRC members with a presence in Nepal. On 26 August 2026, a major ice-rock avalanche occurred in the upper Bhote Koshi watershed near the China–Nepal border, resulting in an historically powerful flash flood that advanced from the border down the entire length of Nepal along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli River basins. This position is being hired to response to the operational requirements of the Flash Flood 2026 response operation, within a Federation-wide operation.

Job Purpose

To manage all IFRC fleet (all assets deployed in operation including IFRC and integrated PNS resources at a country level in-line with Global Fleet Policies & Procedures and Fleet Manual as well as other guidance, standards and processes to ensure a high-quality service provision that meets the needs of the Federation and service users with objectives of safety, environment and fleet management.

Job Duties and Responsibilities

  • Promote the Federation’s fleet management services and VRP to National Societies within the country including access to the VRP and purchasing services, Fleet Wave, end-of-life disposal, management, etc.
  • To be responsible that vehicle fleet is optimized in its size, vehicle models, utilization, running operational costs and is used as per set rules and regulations described in Fleet Manual.
  • To ensure timely, accurate and correct data entry into the fleet management system and to maintain vehicle fleet files with containing documentation with records of mileage, fuel, maintenance and repairs, accidents, and financial information as per Fleet Manual and set procedures.
  •  To plan, allocate and co-ordinate local driver resources to ensure the most effective use of their time and the efficient delivery of transport services using available resourcing and route planning tools as appropriate to minimize the costs of such resources.
  •  To provide support in testing, training of national fleet management staff, volunteers, and National Societies (NS) to improve the management of quality and cost effectiveness of fleet management operations, promote adherence to best practice principles and compliance with all relevant regulation, legislation and IFRC Fleet Manual
  •  To ensure that the necessary information related to transport/fleet management is effectively shared and communicated to the Sr. Logistics Officer and all other relevant IFRC functions e. g. on driver/vehicle movements/fleet performance/driving safety and accidents
  • Ability to focus and identify high Risk areas and put in place risk management control measures
  •  To support the Country Sr. Logistics Officer in managing, evaluating, and reporting upon fleet management activity/performance to verify the meeting of delivery and quality targets, in-line with GLS and country strategies, and accurate and timely cost information to enable the full recovery of all relevant cost from internal/external service users.
  •  Ensure efficient dispatch of fleet resources to meet program needs in line with standing IFRC fleet manual guidelines ensuring optimum resource utilization
  •  Managing Fleet Assistant, dispatchers, and drivers, providing training, coaching and mentoring as well as all HR related tasks including leave planning, discipline and staff appraisals

Organizational Context

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability. IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe. The IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. The IFRC is currently present in Nepal through a Country Delegation (CD – first established in 1965 with a presence through regional representation at times), providing support to Nepal Red Cross Society (NRCS) programmes and National Society development (NSD) amongst as well as emergency response, other areas. The longer-term mission of the Nepal Delegation is to facilitate organisational growth, technical capacities, partnerships, and resource mobilisation that enable Nepal Red Cross Society to deliver on its humanitarian mandate in the country through the provision of technical support, advocacy, representation and coordination functions, in accordance with Strategy 2030, the IFRC Renewal and annual Operational Plans. The Country Delegation also provides integration services to six IFRC members with a presence in Nepal. On 26 August 2026, a major ice-rock avalanche occurred in the upper Bhote Koshi watershed near the China–Nepal border, resulting in an historically powerful flash flood that advanced from the border down the entire length of Nepal along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli River basins. This position is being hired to response to the operational requirements of the Flash Flood 2026 response operation, within a Federation-wide operation.

Job Purpose

This position is focused on providing support to Country Delegation Nepal and movement partners in Nepal in the area of Procurement; the incumbent is considered an integral part of the support system of Nepal Red Cross Society both in the assigned sector as well as the overall capacity building of the National Society. As such it is expected that the incumbent works cooperatively with NRCS when called upon to support.

Job Duties and Responsibilities

  • Ensure and focus to plan, co-ordinate and organize country level IFRC procurement activities in full compliance with IFRC Procurement Procedures and best practices to enable a high quality, efficient and cost-effective procurement process that meets the requests of the services users.
  • Assist and guide to procurement colleagues in maintaining International Federation standard procurement practices keeping records to full audit trail standard.
  •  Support on all types of Local Procurement activities and its supply chain management and also procurement planning with detail mapping and forecasting on procurement.
  • Provide Procurement progress updates timely manner.
  • Ensure with all the LR- specifications and scope of work in coordination with requester and delegate some of the requisitioning/Procurement to Logistics officer.
  •  Plan, co-ordinate and organize country level IFRC procurement activities in full compliance with IFRC Procurement procedures and best practices to enable a high quality, efficient, and cost -effective procurement process that meets the requester requirement.
  •  Provide suggestions, feedback and advice wherever require on procurement and other logistics issue for IFRC, PNSs and NRCS as well.
  • Coach and provide technical tips to Logistics Officer as well as NS and PNS Procurement colleagues on Procurement processes, way forward and training/orientation wherever requires.
  •  Supervise, monitor and review on all the documents for Procurement processes which NRCS commence under IFRC budgets and ensure its compliance with IFRC Procurement manual.
  •  Participate Procurement planning meetings and provide Procurement update report as and when required to IFRC management. And monthly reports to Global Humanitarian Service and Supply Chain Management- Asia Pacific, Kuala Lumpur & Global Humanitarian Service and Supply Chain Management-Dubai.
  • Ensure in obtaining minimum three quotations, preparation of a Comparative Bid Analysis, and advise in recommending purchasing, with all information being systematically recorded in Purchase Committee minutes where appropriate.
  • Ensure that the preparation and submission of appropriate supporting documents to the Committee on Contracts at the National level
  •  Ensure in liaising with relevant field level operational partners and governmental bodies and keep up to date with local market conditions/survey/assessment to enable delivery of most efficient procurement service.
  •  Liaise with suppliers, service providers and other relevant stakeholders regarding delivery of supplies or services and keeping all parties informed of any changes in a timely manner.
  •  Prepare and present procurement files to local Committee of Contracts and submit required documents to/through Global Humanitarian Services and Supply Chain Management (GHSSCM), Asia Pacific, Kuala Lumpur for technical approvals/GVA CoC approval.

Job Duties and Responsibilities (continued)

  •  Ensure that quality control/checks are conducted for all items, materials, or tools procured and delivered by suppliers, that they all meet specifications stated in contracts, are fit for the intended purpose, and have appropriate inspection certificates, when required.
  • To carry accountability for ensuring that all procured goods and services are compliant with IFRC regulations and quality standards, are fit for purpose and inspection compliant.

Who are we?

As a global leader, CARE is shaping the future of the humanitarian and development sector. Each year, we deliver support and services to millions of people in over a hundred countries. We do this by focusing on our mission and living the values that drive our organization. A career at CARE is an opportunity to be part of a movement that brings communities together to solve complex problems and foster lasting change throughout the world. We seek individuals who are passionate about humanitarian and development work, collaborate well with others, embrace learning and innovation, and deliver results.

CARE has been operational in Nepal since 1978 and works in partnerships with government and non-government stakeholders across the spectrum of humanitarian action and long-term development programs. We create local solutions to poverty and inequality and seek dignity for everyone every day and during times of crisis. CARE puts women and girls at the center of everything we do because they have proven to be the best hope for creating lasting change in the world.

Start Fund Nepal is a Start Network programme and is hosted by CARE – Nepal. SFN is a collectively managed financing mechanism, developed in Nepal by international (15 INGOs) Start Network members and partner NGOs (16 LNGOs) based in Nepal with support from the global Start Fund. SFN was launched in June 2021, with the support from the UK Foreign Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) and its first pilot year ended in March 2022 after which the exposure and coverage of the fund has grown significantly. Its pilot project was completed in March 2022. Phase II of the project started in April 2022 and will conclude in March 2024. Following global guidelines, Start Fund Nepal adheres to a 45-day implementation cycle, ensuring swift decision-making within 72 hours of a crisis alert and initiating primary activities within 7 days. Thus, the fund’s primary focus lies in rapid financing and response. Recently, Start Fund Nepal has expanded its scope with the introduction of the Forecast-based, Warning, Analysis, and Response Network (FOREWARN) within its Crisis Anticipation and Risk Financing Unit. This initiative aims to engage non-member, multi-disciplinary actors in Nepal involved in disaster risk analysis and management, particularly in crisis anticipation and early action. FOREWARN aims to facilitate the quick assembly of experts to forecast disasters and provide support to humanitarian efforts in the vicinity of anticipated crises. Additionally, FOREWARN advocates for the normalization of early action in disaster response protocols.

Position: Data and Platform Manager
Vacancy: 7714
Unit: Biodiversity Assessment and Knowledge
Organisation: International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)
Location: Nepal Country Office, Kathmandu, Nepal
Reporting to: Programme Manager, Red List of Ecosystems – Biodiversity Assessment and Knowledge Team
Work percentage: 100%
Grade: P2
Expected start date: 01 November 2026
Type of contract: Fixed-term (up to 24 months with possibility of renewal)
Closing date: 12 October 2026

BACKGROUND

IUCN, in collaboration with the University of Melbourne and several Red List of Ecosystems partners, is rebuilding the Red List of Ecosystems (RLE) data platform. The new system will support the storage, management, and dissemination of RLE data, enable the timely delivery of new assessments, and improve the use of results for decision-making.

The development phase will focus on:

  • Streamlining workflows for data ingestion, storage, validation, and publication.
  • Enhancing the user experience to improve access to existing assessments and accelerate the production of new ones.
  •  Integrating AI and machine-learning methods, where appropriate, to support analysis and assessment processes.
  •  Ensuring interoperability with related systems, including other IUCN data products such as the Red List of Threatened Species and relevant external systems.

The Data & Platform Manager – Red List of Ecosystems, will play a central role in shaping the overall vision for the Red List of Ecosystems (RLE) data platform. This new system will support the storage, management, and dissemination of RLE data, enable the timely delivery of new assessments, and improve the use of results for decision-making. The position will be key in coordinating with partners and stakeholders and driving the delivery of the IUCN RLE platform.
The purpose of this position is to lead product strategy, planning, and execution for the Red List of Ecosystems digital platform, encompassing both web development and data management. The role ensures that the platform meets user needs, aligns with IUCN’s strategic priorities, and adheres to responsible AI practices and robust data governance standards.
The Data & Platform Manager – Red List of Ecosystems will also work closely with the IUCN Conservation Informatics team (including the Red List Data Manager and the Red List Systems Manager), the IUCN Program Manager for the Red List of Ecosystems, and a range of external collaborators from partner institutions to achieve these goals.

JOB DESCRIPTION

The Data & Platform Manager – Red List of Ecosystems will be responsible for the development, maintenance, and long-term sustainability of the Red List of Ecosystems (RLE) database and associated digital platforms. The role combines IT product management and data management functions, working closely with scientific teams, IT partners, and external data providers.

1.Product Strategy & Roadmapping

  • Develop, maintain and update a long-term product roadmap for the Red List of Ecosystem’s digital platform, data infrastructure, and AI-assisted tools, ensuring sustainability beyond immediate project cycles.
  • Define and articulate product vision, success metrics, and phased delivery plans for platform development, maintenance, and evolution.
  •  Facilitate workshops with stakeholders and partners to align priorities.
  •  Prioritise features and technical enhancements using measurable criteria (impact, feasibility, risk, scalability, data maturity, AI readiness).
  • Ensure alignment with IUCN’s digital transformation policies, the Conservation Data Hub vision, and interoperability between Red List of Ecosystems and other IUCN data products like the Red List of Threatened Species
  •  Contribute to planning for long-term platform resourcing, technical debt management, and lifecycle management of software and data assets.

2. Requirements Gathering & User Experience

  •  Manage external consultant work/service provision, on user research, system design or technical development ensuring to translate outputs into formal requirements and user stories.
  •  Map end-to-end data flows: ingestion, validation, versioning, assessment, review and publication.
  •  Ensure user-centred design principles are applied, with strong attention to accessibility, usability, multilingual support, and varying technical capacities of global users.
  •  Maintain up-to-date system and data flow documentation to support onboarding, knowledge transfer, and long-term maintainability.

3 AI & Data Functionality

  • Identify, assess and prioritize use cases where AI/ML can support RLE processes
    (e.g., automated data checks, geospatial anomaly detection, ecological similarity modelling, NLP support for documentation).
  •  Collaborate with scientists and developers to design safe and transparent AI features.
  • Define evaluation metrics and quality assurance processes for AI supported functions.
  •  Support the design and development of data pipelines, , metadata standards, and data models
  •  Contribute to development of embedding, Model Context Protocols (MCP), Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and any other AI standards and techniques where appropriate.

4 Project Coordination & Delivery

  •  Coordinate with partners the product backlog, sprint planning, and release schedules.
  • Coordinate activities across software developers, DevOps, data engineers, and scientific contributors.
  • Oversee integration with existing IUCN systems.
  •  Monitor delivery progress, dependencies, and risks, and proactively address delays or resource constraints.

5 Data Management, Governance, Risks & Compliance

  •  Act as data steward for the RLE database, ensuring high standards of data quality, consistency, completeness, and documentation.
  •  Establish and maintain data governance processes, including data standards, validation rules, version control, audit trails, and long-term archiving strategies.
  •  Ensure appropriate data sharing agreements, licences, and permissions are in place with partners and contributors, in line with IUCN policies and international best practice.
  •  Define a data governance framework with the definition of accountability and standard processes for monitoring data quality.
  • Establish data security policies with different degrees of protection according to different categories and with role definition that defines access
  • Champion data integrity creating procedures to protect the Red List of Ecosystems data from data loss and inaccuracies.
  • Set up a data and disaster recovery plan.
  •  Ensure compliance with IUCN data policies, responsible AI guidelines, and privacy/ethics principles.
  •  Identify and mitigate risks related to data quality, cybersecurity, AI bias, and system reliability.
  •  Maintain documentation of data models, APIs, standards, and governance decisions.

6 Stakeholder Engagement

  • Coordinate consultations, feedback sessions, and user-testing cycles to continuously improve platform functionality and data workflows.
  •  Communicate product decisions and rationales clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  •  Support capacity building by contributing to guidance materials, training resources, and best-practice documentation for data contributors and users.

REQUIREMENTS

Essential

  • Undergraduate degree or equivalent work experience in computer science, information systems, environmental science or a related field.
  • Demonstrated minimum of 8 years of professional experience in product management, technical coordination, or data management for digital platforms, particularly data-intensive or analytics-enabled systems. Experience of minimum 2 years within a multinational environment
  • Solid working knowledge of data management and governance practices, including data quality control, validation workflows, documentation, versioning, and data sharing arrangements.
  • Experience contributing to or supporting AI- or automation-enabled functionalities
  • Ability to translate scientific or domain-expert requirements into clear technical requirements, user stories, or system specifications.
  • Experience working with multidisciplinary teams (e.g. developers, data engineers, scientists, UX or data specialists) and coordinating contributions from internal and external partners.
  • Strong communication, organisational, and prioritisation skills, with the ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders in an international context.
  • Experience working in an Agile environment.
  • Fluency in one IUCN official language and local language.

Desirable

  • Experience with conservation, biodiversity, ecosystem, or environmental data systems.
  • Familiarity with geospatial data and GIS concepts, including spatial databases or APIs.
  • Working knowledge of cloud-hosted platforms and modern data infrastructures.
  • Exposure to large language models (LLMs), AI-assisted data workflows, or advanced data integration approaches (e.g. RAG, vector databases).
  • Familiarity with the IUCN Red List of Ecosystems and/or Red List of Threatened Species processes.
  • Experience working in an international, non-profit, or mission-driven organisation.

This position is based at IUCN Nepal Country Office, and only Nepali citizens are eligible to apply.

APPLICATIONS

Applicants are requested to apply online through the HR Management System, by opening the vacancy announcement and pressing the “Apply” button.

Applicants will be asked to create an account and submit their profile information. Applications will not be accepted after the closing date. The vacancy closes at midnight, Swiss time (GMT+1 / GMT+2 during Daylight Saving Time, DST). Please note that only selected applicants will be personally contacted for interviews.

Other job opportunities are published in the IUCN website: https://www.iucn.org/involved/jobs/

About IUCN

IUCN is a membership Union uniquely composed of both government and civil society organisations. It provides public, private and non-governmental organisations with the knowledge and tools that enable human progress, economic development and nature conservation to take place together.

Created in 1948, IUCN is now the world’s largest and most diverse environmental network, harnessing the knowledge, resources and reach of more than 1,400 Member organisations and around 16,000 experts. It is a leading provider of conservation data, assessments and analysis. Its broad membership enables IUCN to fill the role of incubator and trusted repository of best practices, tools and international standards.

IUCN provides a neutral space in which diverse stakeholders including governments, NGOs, scientists, businesses, local communities, indigenous peoples organisations and others can work together to forge and implement solutions to environmental challenges and achieve sustainable development.

Working with many partners and supporters, IUCN implements a large and diverse portfolio of conservation projects worldwide. Combining the latest science with the traditional knowledge of local communities, these projects work to reverse habitat loss, restore ecosystems and improve people’s well-being.

Background:

Micronutrient deficiency has detrimental effects on health, learning ability, and productivity and may lead to high social and public costs, reduced productivity in populations due to high rates of illness, disability, and loss of human potential. Food fortification plays a crucial role in reducing micronutrient deficiency by enhancing the nutritional value of commonly consumed foods. This cost-effective and sustainable strategy has the potential to positively impact the health and well-being of individuals, particularly in countries like Nepal where prevalence of micronutrient deficiency is high.

At the same time, millet is a nutrient-rich and climate-resilient crop with strong potential to address Nepal’s persistent micronutrient deficiencies. Recognizing this opportunity, WFP, in partnership with the Government of Nepal (GoN), academia, and the private sector, plans to strengthen millet and sorghum value chains, generate evidence on their nutritional benefits, develop enrichment standards, and promote consumption through Social and Behaviour Change (SBC) initiatives. Through research, product innovation, market development, and integration into school meals and community nutrition programmes, the initiative aims to make nutritious millet-based products more accessible, affordable, and appealing to Nepali households. Through these efforts, WFP will contribute to Country Strategic Plan’s Outcome 2 by improving nutrition outcomes and access to nutritious diets, and to Outcome 3 by supporting climate-resilient food systems, sustainable livelihoods, and local value chain development.

Purpose of the Assignment:

To advance WFP Nepal’s food fortification agenda, WFP seeks a Programme Associate (Micronutrients) who will work under the direct supervision of the Programme Policy Officer (Nutrition Lead) at the Country Office (CY). The incumbent will provide technical, operational, and coordination support to strengthen the implementation and scale-up of rice, millet, and sorghum fortification initiatives in Nepal.

Based at the WFP Country Office, the incumbent will serve for coordinating and supporting fortification-related activities, including quality assurance and monitoring systems, policy and technical discussions, capacity strengthening initiatives, and evidence generation. The assignment aims to promote the sustainable mainstreaming of fortified rice, millet, and sorghum within Nepal’s food system through strengthened partnerships, enhanced institutional capacities, effective knowledge management, and evidence-based implementation, ultimately contributing to improved nutrition outcomes, resilient local food systems, and greater climate resilience.

Shaanxi Construction Engineering Group Corporation Limited, is a leading state-owned enterprise in international civil infrastructure development, invites applications from highly qualified and experienced professionals for the senior leadership position of Head of Communications and Operations for its Nepal Branch office. The successful candidate will lead the planning, coordination, supervision and oversight of equipment repair and maintenance operations across the Group’s road, bridge, building, and municipal infrastructure projects, while serving as the principal communications interface between head office and offices globally, site operations, project departments, contractors, consultants, employers, and regulatory bodies on all matters relating to construction procurement and contract administration.

Qualification

  • Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Architectural Engineering, Construction Engineering, Mechanical/Construction Equipment Engineering, or a closely related field from a recognized university; a Master’s degree in Construction Management, Civil Engineering, or MBA is preferred.

Managerial & Sector Experience

  •  Minimum 10 years of demonstrable managerial/supervisory experience within construction engineering, equipment maintenance, or infrastructure project operations, including progressive advancement through roles such as Technician, Building/Section Supervisor, Technical Manager, Project/Deputy Project Manager, and Regional or Production Manager.
  • Proven track record leading multi-project equipment maintenance and operations functions concurrently across several active construction sites (residential, municipal, industrial, and public-welfare/resettlement projects), including responsibility for tower cranes, hoists, concrete pumping equipment, mixing plants, and steel-structure processing machinery.
  •  Minimum 15 years of overall experience in the construction sector, with a demonstrated career progression from field/technical roles into managerial and regional leadership positions. Direct experience developing and implementing preventive and corrective maintenance plans, equipment inspection regimes, and downtime-reduction strategies on award-winning or nationally recognized projects.
  •  Demonstrated ability to mentor and supervise technical staff, maintain zero-incident safety records, and ensure full compliance with factory/manufacturer technical standards and operating procedures.

Operations Responsibilities (Repair & Maintenance Oversight)

  • Oversee day-to-day and emergency repair and maintenance operations for all construction machinery and equipment across active project sites, cross country operations ensuring minimal downtime and adherence to manufacturer and industry best-practice maintenance standards (e.g., ISO 55000 asset management principles, OEM maintenance protocols, RCM/preventive maintenance frameworks).
  •  Establish and maintain a centralized maintenance log, equipment lifecycle register, and key-performance-indicator (KPI) reporting system covering equipment availability, mean time to repair (MTTR), and mean time between failures (MTBF).
  • Ensure occupational health and safety compliance in all maintenance and repair activities, consistent with international best practice (e.g., ISO 45001) and host-country labour and safety regulations.

Communication & Procurement Responsibilities

  • Serve as the primary communications and coordination focal point on matters relating to construction procurement, tendering, and contract administration under the FIDIC contract suite (Red Book, Yellow Book, Silver Book, and MDB Harmonised Edition), including correspondence on claims, variations, extensions of time, and dispute resolution (DAB/DAAB) processes.
  • Draft, review, and manage formal project correspondence, progress and incident reports, and stakeholder communications with employers, engineers, consultants, subcontractors, and regulatory authorities, in accordance with internationally recognized standards and world-renowned procurement frameworks (World Bank, ADB, AIIB, and comparable multilateral development bank guidelines).
  •  Maintain consistent, transparent, and timely information flow between head office, site operations, project management, head office, and external stakeholders, ensuring alignment between maintenance/operational status and contractual/procurement obligations.
  • Support bid preparation, negotiation, and contract close-out documentation for equipment- and operations-related procurement, ensuring compliance with corporate governance and international best practice.
  •  Represent the Group in communications with government bodies, industry associations, and community stakeholders, upholding the corporate reputation and brand of Shaanxi Construction Engineering Group.

Contractual & Technical Expertise

  •  Working knowledge of the FIDIC contract suite and internationally recognized construction procurement and safeguard standards, sufficient to support project departments in matters of claims, variations, and contract compliance. Familiarity with international construction law, occupational safety regulations, and environmental/social compliance frameworks applicable to civil, municipal, and building infrastructure projects.

Language Requirements (Mandatory)

  • Fluent in Chinese and English — written and spoken — to full professional proficiency.

Strong Leadership & Managerial Competencies, Crisis Management, Stakeholder Coordination, Negotiation, and Report-Writing Skills etc.

How To Apply

KIRDARC Nepal is a non-governmental organization (NGO) dedicated to promoting the rights of marginalized and excluded communities through interventions in human rights, democracy, good governance, and inclusive development. The organization works to strengthen the capacities of rights holders, duty bearers, and civil society organizations to advance social justice, equitable access to opportunities and resources, and sustainable community development.

KIRDARC Nepal is implementing the “Bhotekoshi Flood Emergency Response” project in Rasuwa District, with support from World Vision International Nepal. The Emergency Relief and Early Recovery Project aims to provide timely emergency assistance to approximately 2,500 flood-affected households in Nuwakot District, prioritizing vulnerable and marginalized groups. The project focuses on food security, emergency shelter, WASH, and protection, along with community engagement, accountability, coordination, and post-distribution monitoring, in coordination with relevant government authorities and World Vision International Nepal.

To ensure the effective implementation of this project, KIRDARC Nepal invites applications from qualified, competent, self-motivated, and committed Nepali citizens to fill the following full-time positions:

1. Project Manager-Response – 1 Position based in Rsuwa

Academic Qualification and Experience: Applicants must have a degree in Disaster Management, Social Science, Development Studies, or a related field. Minimum 5 years of experience in managing humanitarian emergency response projects, with at least 2 years in a senior management role in NGO/INGO or development projects.

Key Skills and Knowledge required:- Strong leadership, team management, communication, and negotiation skills; ability to work under pressure and make critical decisions; fluency in Nepali and English, with Tamang or other local Rasuwa languages desirable; and willingness to travel extensively and stay in basic field accommodation.

For more details, visit the detailed job description here.

2. Response Coordinator – 1 Positions based in Rasuwa

Academic Qualification and Experience: Applicants should have a bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (e.g., Public Health, Environment science, Development Studies). Minimum 4 years of experience in the humanitarian sector, with at least 2 years in a supervisory or coordination role.

Key Skills and Knowledge required:– Applicants should have strong leadership, coordination, communication, and report-writing skills, Strong understanding of emergency response standards (Sphere). Familiarity with the geographic and cultural context of the Rasuwa district.

For more details, visit the detailed job description here.

3. Distribution and Cash Voucher Coordinator – 1 Positions based in Rasuwa

Academic Qualification and Experience: Applicants should have a master’s degree in management (specializing in Finance or Accounting) with at least 2 years of relevant experience, or a bachelor’s degree in finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field with at least 5 years of relevant experience.

Key Skills and Knowledge required:– Applicants should have proven experience at least 4 years of humanitarian sector experience, including expertise in Cash and Voucher Assistance (CVA), CTP modalities, and FSPs in Nepal. Experience in emergency NFI/food distribution and proficiency in Excel, KoBo Toolbox, or similar data management tools is required.

For more details, visit the detailed job description here.

4. Finance and Administration Coordinator – 1 Positions based in Rasuwa

Academic Qualification and Experience: Applicants should have a bachelor’s degree in accounting, Finance, or a related field. A professional qualification like CA, ACCA, or CPA is an asset. Proven experience in managing budgets of significant size in an emergency response context.Strong knowledge of accounting software and advanced Excel skills.

Key Skills and Knowledge required:– High integrity, honesty, and ethical standards, with strong attention to detail, accuracy, analytical and problem-solving skills. Ability to work independently, manage multiple tasks, and communicate fluently in Nepali and English.

For more details, visit the detailed job description here.

5. Supply Chain Coordinator – 1 Positions based in Sanepa, Lalitpur

Academic Qualification and Experience: bachelor’s degree in supply chain management, Logistics, Business Administration, or a related field. Minimum 4 years of experience in logistics and procurement, with at least 2 years in an emergency response setting.

Key Skills and Knowledge required:- Sound knowledge and proven experience in managing complex supply chains in challenging and emergency contexts, including sourcing, procurement, logistics, inventory, and fleet management, with a good understanding of organizational, donor, and regulatory compliance requirements.

For more details, visit the detailed job description here.

6. Wash Officer – 1 Positions based in Rasuwa

Academic Qualification and Experience: Bachelor’s degree in public health, Environmental Science, Civil/Sanitary Engineering, or a related field. Minimum 3 years of professional experience, with at least 1–2 years in humanitarian emergency WASH response (preferably flood/landslide contexts).

Key Skills and Knowledge required:- Strong technical knowledge of emergency water treatment systems, gravity-flow systems, and participatory hygiene promotion tools (PHAST/CHAST).

For more details, visit the detailed job description here.

7. Livelihood Officer- 1 Positions based in Rasuwa

Academic Qualification and Experience: Applicants should have a bachelor’s degree in agriculture, Economics, Development Studies, Business Administration, or a related field. Minimum 3 years of experience in livelihood recovery, cash-based interventions (CBI), or economic development projects in rural settings.

Key Skills and Knowledge required:- Proven experience in community mobilization, beneficiary targeting, and working with local cooperatives or farmers’ groups. Deep understanding of rural livelihood systems in mountain regions like Rasuwa.

For more details, visit the detailed job description here

8. Education and Protection Officer – 1 Positions based in Rasuwa

Academic Qualification and Experience: Applicants should have a bachelor’s degree in education, Social Work, Psychology, Human Rights, Gender Studies, or a related field. Minimum 3 years of experience in emergency education, child protection, or community protection programming.

Key Skills and Knowledge required:- Familiarity with international standards (Minimum Standards for Child Protection in Humanitarian Action, EiE standards). Empathetic communication skills and fluency in Nepali and English languages

For more details, visit the detailed job description here.

9. Health and Nutrition Officer- 1 Positions based in Rasuwa

Academic Qualification and Experience: Applicants should have a bachelor’s degree in public health, Nursing, Nutrition, or a related medical field (Registered Nurse/Public Health Inspector preferred). Minimum 3 years of experience in public health, emergency health response, or nutrition programming.

Key Skills and Knowledge required:- Strong familiarity with Nepal’s public health system, health posts, and the role of FCHVs. Strong community mobilization and health education skills.

For more details, visit the detailed job description here.

10. Admin/Logistic Officer- 1 Positions based in Rasuwa

Academic Qualification and Experience: Applicants should have a bachelor’s degree in business administration, Management, Supply Chain, or a related field. Minimum 2–3 years of professional experience in administration, logistics, or supply chain management, preferably within an emergency humanitarian context.

Key Skills and Knowledge required:- Strong organizational skills and the ability to multitask under high-pressure conditions.Knowledge of Rasuwa district roads, local transport syndicates, and geography is a strong asset.

For more details, visit the detailed job description here.

11. Communication and Information Officer- 1 Positions based in Sanepa, Lalitpur

Academic Qualification and Experience: Applicants should have a bachelor’s degree in journalism, Mass Communication, Media Studies, Development Studies, or a related field. Minimum 2–3 years of experience in communications, reporting, or public relations, ideally in the humanitarian or development sector.

Key Skills and Knowledge required:- Excellent writing, editing, and storytelling skills in both Nepali and English. Proficiency in multimedia tools (photography, basic video editing, graphic design/infographics).

For more details, visit the detailed job description here.

Interested candidates who meet these criteria should send their Application Letter and KIRDARC Job Application Form to vacancy@kirdarc.org by 29 September 2026, before 5:00 PM. The CV/Resume is not necessary to submit but the prescribed KIRDARC Job Application Form is mandatorily required to apply. The interested candidates can download the KIRDARC Job Application form from here.

Preference will be given to candidates from the local affected communities in Rasuwa and Nuwakot and Dhading district who possess the required skills and experience. Applicants who have been directly affected by the recent Bhotekoshi floods are strongly encouraged to apply. This will be applied to all positions. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Any telephone inquiries/and or attempts to apply undue influence will result in the disqualification of candidates. KIRDARC Nepal reserves the right to reject any application without assigning any reason whatsoever.

Note: The written test will be conducted in person at designated KIRDARC Nepal Cluster Offices. Shortlisted candidates will be informed of the available test locations and may choose the location that is most convenient for them.

Position: Field Coordinator
Location: Anywhere in Nepal where the work needs you | Base: Kathmandu
Mindset: Co-Founder & Problem-Solver | Pace: High Impact | Excuses Tolerated: Zero

Read this before you read the job.

This is not a desk job with occasional field visits. It is a field job with occasional desk time.
In August 2026, when the Bhotekoshi flood swept through Rasuwa, our team was on the ground assessing needs and delivering relief to affected households along the Trishuli corridor. The same week, other colleagues were working with municipalities on waste systems in Madhesh and Lumbini. That is what a normal month at CREASION looks like.
Since 2005, CREASION has recycled over 15000 tons of plastic, reached more than 21,000 young people, built over 1,662 community infrastructures, and handed Waste Mapbooks to nine local governments. None of that happened from an office chair. It happened because a few people refused to accept “it can’t be done here.”
We are looking for one more of those people.

The role in one line

You will be the person who turns a project plan into real change in a real community, and who can prove it with data.

What you will own (Key Result Areas)

1. Field implementation

Deliver 100% of planned field activities in your assigned project areas on schedule each quarter, with any delay reported and a recovery plan submitted within 48 hours.

2. Community and local government relationships

Build working relationships with ward chairs, municipal officials, cooperatives, schools, informal waste workers and women’s groups. Hold at least [4+] structured stakeholder meetings per month and document every agreement in writing.

3. MERL and activity tracking

Maintain the project tracker so that anyone in Kathmandu can see exactly where every activity stands, any day of the week. Submit weekly progress updates every Friday, monthly reports by the 5th, and verified beneficiary data with photos, attendance, and GPS evidence for every activity.

4. Problem solving on the spot

When a partner cancels, a road closes or a budget line runs short, you find the next best path and inform your supervisor with options, not just the problem.

5. Rapid response readiness

Be deployable within 72 hours to any district during a disaster or emergency response.

6. Stories and evidence

Capture at least two documented case stories per month that show what changed in people’s lives, not just what activity took place.

Who we are looking for

You have worked at grassroots level before, whether through an NGO, a cooperative, a youth club, a campaign or your own initiative. You can sit on the floor of a community hall and speak with the same respect you would give a minister. You know how to run a meeting, keep a register, use a spreadsheet, and send a clear report from your phone.
You are stubborn in the right way. When something is blocked, you go back the next day. You care deeply about Nepal’s environment and its people, and you want your work to be measurable.
Minimum requirements: Bachelor’s degree in Development Studies, Environmental Science, Social Work, Rural Development or a related field, with at least [2] years of field experience. Fluent Nepali required; Maithili, Bhojpuri, Tharu, Tamang or another local language is a real advantage. Two wheeler license and ability to ride on rough roads is required.

This job is NOT for you if

You need a fixed location and fixed hours. You wait to be told what to do next. You think reporting is someone else’s job. You see a remote municipality as a punishment posting. You explain why something didn’t happen before you try to make it happen.
We say this plainly because we would rather lose a hundred applicants than hire one wrong person.

What you get

A chance to do work you can point to for the rest of your life. Direct exposure to the board and senior leadership, with the freedom to shape how projects are delivered. Real responsibility from week one. A team that treats you as a co-builder of the organization, not a staff number. Competitive salary, field allowance, insurance, and a clear growth path to Project Officer for those who deliver.

How to apply (please read carefully)

We do not want a generic cover letter.

1. – Your CV (maximum two pages)
2. – A written answer of no more than 300 words to this question:
“Tell us about something you finished when everyone around you had given up. What did you do, and what was the result?”
3. – One photo from a field activity you led, with two lines explaining it

Send to jobs@creasion.org with the subject line “Field Coordinator_[Your Name]”:

Deadline: October 5, 2026

Shortlisted candidates will spend one day with our team in the field. That day will count more than the interview.
CREASION is an equal opportunity for an employer. Women, persons from marginalized communities and candidates from outside Kathmandu are strongly encouraged to apply.

Position: Senior Project Coordinator – UPLIFT Project

The Opportunity

Save the Children believes every child deserves a future. In Bhutan and around the world, we give children a healthy start in life, the opportunity to learn and protection from harm. We do whatever it takes for children – every day and in times of crisis – transforming their lives and future we share. Save the Children expects that anyone associated with it abides by its Safeguarding and other Zero Tolerance Policies.

The position holder will provide strategic, technical, and managerial leadership for the UPLIFT Project, building on the successes and lessons learned from the POWER 4 AY project, funded by Save the Children Italy. The position is responsible for ensuring the effective implementation of the project through strong program leadership, cross-functional coordination, and effective partnership management with government agencies and partner NGOs (PNGOs) under the Surkhet Field Office

Under the supervision of the Head of Field Program Operations (HoFPOs) and with technical guidance from the Livelihoods Specialist, the position holder will establish and maintain strong coordination with key support functions, including Finance, Logistics, PDQI, POD, and MEAL, at both the Field Office and Country Office levels, as well as with the Bhutan team. The position will ensure timely, effective, and high-quality project implementation through close cross-functional collaboration, proactive coordination, and efficient operational support.

The position holder will ensure the development and implementation of high-quality, results-oriented project plans and ensure effective stakeholder coordination at the field level. The position will foster strategic engagement with the private sector to enhance youth employability through vocational training, micro-enterprise development, and innovative livelihood approaches. The position holder will also establish and oversee robust monitoring systems throughout the project cycle to ensure quality implementation, evidence-based decision-making, accountability, and the timely achievement of project outcomes.

The position holder is responsible for ensuring full compliance with Save the Children International’s (SCI) and donor policies, procedures, and standards throughout the project lifecycle, while adhering to the technical guidance and implementation requirements of Save the Children Italy.

The position holder will be responsible for preparing and submitting high-quality project plans, progress reports, quality review reports, and associated action plans to Save the Children Italy (SC Italy) and other relevant stakeholders, as required. In close coordination with the Country Office Award Management team, the position holder will serve as the primary focal point for communication and coordination with the SC Italy Desk.

The position holder will foster an enabling and collaborative environment that empowers partner organizations to effectively implement project activities, ensuring quality delivery, timely reporting, and compliance with project standards. The position holder will strengthen collaboration with government counterparts, the private sector, and other key stakeholders to maximize project outcomes, promote sustainability, and enhance benefits for target groups. Effective partnership management of the SC Italy-funded project is a key responsibility of this position.

In addition, the position holder will work together with Bhutan Office to develop consolidated project report on annual basis ensuring quality and donor standards.

KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY:

Planning & Budgeting

  • Lead the planning processes and ensures partners have detailed implementation plan including realistic phased budget outlining major activities and timeline for the funds allocated in required planning templates provided by the organization.
  • Ensures appropriate fund allocation and expenditure monthly and take corrective measures by revisiting plans and communicating timely with technical advisor, finance and Award team.
  • Reviews the project’s BVAs and reports on any discrepancies identified in comparison to the Program BVA shared by the Finance team monthly.
  • Monthly monitoring of fund allocation and expenditure, identify variances, and take corrective actions through plan revisions and timely coordination with Technical Advisors and relevant departments.
  • Coordinates with SCI and partner team to design a robust field visit plan, self-assessments and monitoring systems including follow up on recommendations with relevant department and impact areas.
  • Leads the revision of budgets during budget forecast and on exchange rate fluctuations as per organizational procedures.
  • Prepare and implement a private sector engagement plan, including collaboration with business incubators, based on the findings and recommendations of the market assessment and private sector mapping.
  • Coordinates with Thematic Specialist and Advisors for technical assistance, as required.

Technical Assistance and Quality Assurance:

  • Provide oversight and ensure quality of programmes in the field ensure its optimum benefit to the vulnerable population.
  • Provide technical support to implementing partners to ensure the quality implementation of project activities related to private sector-led job placement and incubation-supported micro-enterprise development, while promoting climate-resilient, green job standards and sustainable livelihood practices.
  • Conduct regular field visits to partner organisations and areas, check and ensure the quality, identify best practices, identify issues to be addressed, and share any issues with the technical advisor to seek solutions/alternatives
  • Coordinate to ensure that all project implementation materials /guidelines are reviewed by relevant technical team
  • Provide technical support to implementing partners on life skills, business incubation approaches, enterprise development, business promotion and marketing, green jobs and green
  • skills, and other emerging approaches and cross-cutting issues related to livelihoods promotion and youth employability.
  • Ensure that project quality benchmarks and standards are established, finalized jointly with MEAL, Technical Advisors, and partners, and consistently applied across all levels of implementation.

Programme Operations & Management

  • Lead market assessments, livelihood opportunity mapping, private sector engagement, and onboarding of strategic private sector partners for the project.
  • Ensures programmatic and financial accountability including tracking of program progress and budget expense in the use of funds and achievement of all related projects, in alignment with Annual Plan and Country Strategy Plan.
  • Ensure the program operations manual (POM) and its components are prepared, understood by relevant staff, and kept in place for monitoring.
  • Ensure and collect the information about project progress from field staff, analyse the expenses Vs activity delivery and submit to Supervisor in a monthly basis.
  • Ensures that programs meet KPIs and /or excels Minimum Operating Standards of key programmatic interventions including Gender and Social Inclusion principles.

Innovation and Scale

  • Identifies best practices, problems and issues around program implementation and works toward finding solutions for improvements, documenting, disseminating and in consultation with relevant departments and themes.
  • Coordinates with Thematic coordinators/ managers/Specialists, TA providers to promote and pilot innovations in program areas as relevant.
  • Contributes towards developing and implementation of new ideas/innovations and its documentation of processes and its results, based on learning from Nepal’s experience.
  • Ensures effective monitoring and evaluations are carried out for deriving lessons learned, best practices and that monitoring is effective in terms of deriving quick analysis of progresses for immediate corrective actions and measurement of results.
  • Identify and engage potential business incubation center within the project areas and support their onboarding to establish and operationalize AI-enabled incubation services for youth entrepreneurs.

Documentation & Reporting

  • As the project lead, update data and information related to the project in the PRIME system
  • Lead the timely preparation and submission of high-quality project plans, progress reports, quality review reports, and other donor-required documentation to Save the Children
  • International and Save the Children Italy, ensuring that achievements, progress, and learning are accurately reflected.
  • Coordinate closely with the Livelihoods Specialist, MEAL, Communications and Media teams, and implementing partners to ensure effective monitoring, evaluation, documentation, and dissemination of project achievements, lessons learned, and best practices.
  • Work with the MEAL team to ensure the timely completion of baseline, endline, and other project assessments, incorporating feedback from SCI Nepal, SC Italy, and Country Office teams. Collaborate with the MEAL team and the Livelihoods Specialist to establish and validate baseline values and track progress against project indicators.
  • In close collaboration with the Livelihoods Specialist and the MEAL team, generate evidence, learning, and strategic insights to strengthen ongoing implementation, support adaptive management, and inform future program design.
  • Foster a culture of learning, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement by promoting the documentation and exchange of good practices, innovations, and lessons learned across program and partners.
  • Organize and facilitate field visits for Save the Children, donors, government representatives, and other stakeholders
  • Lead in the preparation of high-quality case studies, learning documents, success stories, and technical reports in line with organizational and donor requirements.
  • Keep the Livelihoods Specialist and HOFO regularly informed of project progress, key achievements, emerging issues, risks, and challenges, and seek technical guidance on strategic decisions and implementation approaches.
  • Work closely with programme and support teams to ensure that all narrative reports and project deliverables are prepared and submitted in accordance with Save the Children and donor contractual requirements, agreed timelines, and quality standards.

Partner’s management

  • Lead partnership management by ensuring compliance with partnership agreements, Save the Children policies, donor requirements, zero-tolerance standards, audit recommendations, and management response plans.
  • Ensure that implementing partners clearly understand and comply with all provisions of partnership agreements, as well as Save the Children’s partnership principles, policies, and procedures, to enable effective and accountable project implementation.
  • Assess partners’ organizational and technical capacity needs, particularly in delivering market-driven employability interventions using innovative approaches such as AI-enabled business incubation, job guarantee-linked employment models, and facilitating access to finance for micro-entrepreneurs through venture capital, credit services, and other emerging financing mechanisms. Develop and implement capacity-strengthening plans to address identified gaps.
  • Build and maintain strong working relationships with government counterparts, implementing partners, development partners, donors, private sector actors, and other key stakeholders at the local, district, and provincial levels to ensure effective project implementation and coordination.
  • Work closely with implementing partners to ensure quality, timely, and results-oriented implementation of project activities, while fostering collaboration, joint problem-solving, and continuous learning.
  • Extend coordination and collaboration with government line agencies, NGOs, CSOs, UN agencies, and other relevant stakeholders to promote integrated programming, resource sharing, and synergies in support of children’s rights and youth employability.
  • Represent SCI in relevant sub national coordination forums, technical working groups, networks, and coalitions, ensuring effective representation of field-level priorities and contributing to sectoral learning and collaboration.
  • Engage with government line agencies and relevant programs to promote the institutionalization and scale-up of successful project approaches and contribute to advocacy efforts that influence child-focused and youth-related policies, strategies, and procedures at the local and provincial levels.
  • Build and maintain strong collaborative relationships across SCI departments and teams to ensure effective cross-functional coordination and integrated program delivery.
  • Document and share project learning, innovations, evidence, and good practices through appropriate national and sub-national platforms, in accordance with Save the Children’s communication and knowledge management protocols.
  • Build and maintain strong coordination and collaboration among implementing partners, provincial networks, government line agencies, and other relevant stakeholders to promote integrated implementation, knowledge sharing, and sustainable project outcome

Representation and Networking

Qualifications and Experience:

  • Master’s degree with 4 years of experience (3 years for GSI) on enterprises development/agriculture ; OR Bachelor’s degree with 6 years of experience (4 years for GSI) on enterprise development/agriculture
  • Prior experience in the I/NGO on empowering youth to create economic opportunities through, minimize the impacts of climate change and promote green job and green skills
  • Demonstrated significant experience in managing projects funded by multiple donors including networks.
  • Proven sound strategic thinking and planning skills, including ability to think creatively and be innovative, set priorities, manage work plans and evaluate progress.
  • Good report writing ad communication skill.
  • Good interpersonal skills including verbal and written communication skills.
  • Teamwork and team mobilization skills.

Background and Job Description

Job Description The selected incumbent will be placed in Bidur, Nuwakot, Nepal.

Background The Department of Safety and Security (UNDSS) is responsible for providing leadership, operational support and oversight of the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS) globally. As a global leader in security risk management principles, UNDSS enables the safe and effective delivery of United Nations programmes and activities in the most complex and challenging environments, while maximizing precious resources. To this end, the work of the Department is aligned under a clear mission, to enable United Nations system programme activities through trusted security leadership and solutions.

This is a unique opportunity to join a diverse, dynamic and exciting organization, gaining unique and valuable experience where security provides great value. Besides the opportunity to gain new skills and further advance security expertise, this position offers a fulfilling environment that gives you satisfaction by contributing directly or indirectly to peace and security, human rights, and achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals. Simply, all humanity will benefit from your work. Together, we can make the world a better place.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the direct supervision of the Multi Country Office Security Adviser, the Local Security Assistant supports the implementation of UNSMS security policies, procedures, plans and operational arrangements within the assigned Area of Responsibility. The incumbent assists with security information management, security risk management, emergency preparedness, incident response, security assessments, training, liaison and interagency security coordination within delegated authority. During emergencies or periods of increased operational demand, the incumbent may be required to provide security support in other parts of Nepal, as directed by the MCO Security Adviser.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Assists the MCO Security Adviser in collecting, verifying, updating and communicating information concerning the security situation within the assigned Area of Responsibility.
  • Maintains day-to- day operational coordination with the relevant Area Security Coordinator and provides support on safety and security matters within the assigned Area of Responsibility. Serves as Secretary to the Area Security Management Team, as directed by the MCO Security Adviser.
  • Maintains working level liaison, as appropriate, with relevant national, provincial and local authorities, including police, military, emergency management and other government officials, as well as relevant non-governmental organizations within the assigned Area of Responsibility.
  • Monitors security incidents, developments and trends within the assigned Area of Responsibility. Collects, verifies, collates and evaluates security information and provides verified information and observations to the MCO Security Adviser for analysis and assessment.
  • Communicates verified security information to heads of UN suboffices, Security Focal Points and other authorized recipients through established UNSMS communication channels, as directed or authorized by the MCO Security Adviser.
  • Maintains regular contact with Security Focal Points of UNSMS Organizations, UN Humanitarian Partners, and Host Government security organization in the Region(s).
  • Provides advice and technical assistance on safety and security matters at ASMT meetings on behalf of the MCO-SA.
  • Assists in preparing the Regional Security Plan(s) and implementing the Security Risk Management (SRM) measures, Assists the MCO-SA in monitoring compliance of SRM measures. Also, he/she assists in complying with the SRM measures to UNSMS organizations with the AoR.
  • Assists in reporting security incidents affecting UN personnel, premises, offices, and assets; and assists in the preparation of security reports, such as the SSIRS, and the general Security Assessments.
  • Organizes and conducts security training directed by MCO-SA and provides security orientation briefing to newly assigned staff members within region(s).
  • Maintains updated UNSMS Personnel lists in his/her Region(s)/AoR.
  • Implements SMT approved Residential Security Measures (RSM) for international staff if assigned to the Region(s).
  • Provides support in conducting security evaluations and provides advice on security measures for the residences (Residential Security Measures – RSM) of UN staff, as well as on latest trends and threats to staff safety and security.
  • Keeps updated information related to UN Personnel, offices, premises.
  • Performs any other tasks as assigned by the MCO-SA.
  • Supports emergency preparedness, personnel accountability, Warden arrangements, contingency planning, emergency exercises and emergency response activities. Assists in implementing emergency arrangements during security incidents or crises.
  • Assists in conducting security assessments and inspections of UN premises, residences, programme locations, routes, hotels, event venues and other operational locations. Supports follow up and monitoring of approved recommendations.
  • Supports security arrangements for UN missions, field activities, official visits and significant events, including route and location checks and liaison with relevant authorities.
  • Supports the maintenance and testing of the Security Communications System and emergency communication arrangements. Reports communication gaps or equipment failures and maintains relevant operational records.
  • Supports premises security assessments, access control arrangements, guard force coordination and monitoring of contracted security service providers, where applicable within the assigned Area of Responsibility.
  • Maintains routine and confidential security correspondence, incident records, security assessments, contact databases, meeting records and other operational documentation.
  • Supports security arrangements that take account of the different needs and vulnerabilities of UN personnel and contribute to the inclusion of gender, diversity and accessibility considerations in security preparedness and response activities.
  • Promote a respectful, inclusive, and safe workplace culture through daily interactions, team collaboration, and adherence to organizational policies.
  • The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement The incumbent reports directly to the UNDSS Multi Country Office Security Adviser and maintains day-to-day operational coordination with the relevant Area Security Coordinator. The position requires frequent travel within the assigned Area of Responsibility and deployment elsewhere in Nepal at short notice when operationally required.

Competencies

Core Competencies

  • Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline
  • Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements
  • Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback
  • Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible
  • Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident
  • Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships
  • Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross Functional & Technical competencies

  • Security Services – Security incident management & monitoring: Ability to provide adequate response to security incidents/events
  • Security Services – Security information management: Analytical capabilities to process diverse security information and develop recommendations
  • Security Services – Safety and Security risk management: Ability to assess threats and risks, identify and oversee implementation of mitigation measures, including ability to design and test safety and security plans. including ability to design and test safety and security plans
  • Business Management – Communication: Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels
  • Business Management – Risk Management: Identify and organize action around reducing, mitigating and proactively managing risks
  • 2030 Agenda: Peace – Governance: Inclusion and Participation of Marginalised Groups
  • 2030 Agenda: People – Gender: Innovation for Gender Equality

Required Skills and Experience
