title.rendered: Project Coordinator, Health Supervisor, Staff Nurse, Auxiliary Nurse Midwife (ANM)

content.rendered:
PHASE Nepal is a non-governmental, non-profit, non-political and non-religious organization established in 2006 with a vision of building a self-empowered and self-sustained society free from discrimination. PHASE Nepal works in the areas of health, education, livelihoods, research, disability inclusion and community development across different districts of Nepal.

A sudden flood on 26 August 2026 caused significant disruption along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridors following an ice and rock collapse near the Nepal–China border. The disaster affected communities, infrastructure and essential services in the affected areas.

PHASE Nepal has initiated emergency relief support and is strengthening its response to address the health and other urgent needs of affected communities in coordination with local governments, health authorities, community representatives and other relevant stakeholders.

To support the continuation of these emergency response activities, PHASE Nepal invites applications from qualified, motivated and committed candidate for the following positions:

Duty Station: Assigned Health Post, Rasuwa District

Contract Duration: Initially one year, with the possibility of extension subject to organizational requirements, performance and availability of funding.

Position: Project Coordinator
No. of Vacancy: 1
Minimum Education: Bachelor’s degree in Public Health or equivalent from a recognized institution
Experience: Minimum 3 years of relevant experience, including experience in health program coordination or humanitarian/emergency response
Salary (Gross/Month) Rs. 80,272

Position: Health Supervisor
No. of Vacancy: 2
Minimum Education: Health Assistant (HA) completed from a recognized institution, with valid registration with the relevant professional council
Experience: Minimum 2 years of relevant experience in clinical settings, including patient care, safer motherhood, newborn care, HMIS recording, reporting and documentation
Salary (Gross/Month) Rs. 76,371

Position: Staff Nurse
No. of Vacancy: 2
Minimum Education: PCL Nursing/Bachelor’s in Nursing with valid registration with Nepal Nursing Council
Experience: Minimum 2 year of relevant nursing experience. Experience in hospital, health facility, community health, emergency response or humanitarian settings will be preferred
Salary (Gross/Month) Rs. 76,371

Position: Auxiliary Nurse Midwife (ANM)
No. of Vacancy: 2
Minimum Education: ANM qualification from a recognized institution with valid registration with Nepal Nursing Council
Experience: Relevant experience in maternal and child health, maternity and delivery services, community health or emergency response. SBA training will be preferred.
Salary (Gross/Month) Rs. 66,903

Note: The above-mentioned gross monthly salary is inclusive of Social Security Fund (SSF), festival allowance, food allowance and field allowance.

Key Responsibilities

1. Project Coordinator

  • Coordinate emergency health and program activities with local level authorities, and PHASE team.
  • Identify program needs, gaps and resource requirements and communicate them to the PHASE team.
  • Develop, implement and monitor activity plans and ensure timely follow-up.
  • Monitor field activities, health service delivery, coverage, referrals and overall program progress.
  • Coordinate the availability of required medicines, supplies, equipment and other program resources.
  • Maintain proper program records, data and documentation and prepare timely reports for PHASE team.
  • Prepare and submit reports in accordance with government and PHASE Nepal reporting formats and requirements.
  •  Support assessments, community engagement, coordination meetings and emergency response activities.
  •  Follow up with local stakeholders and PHASE teams on identified issues, requirements and agreed actions.
  • Provide necessary support during periods of staff unavailability to ensure continuity of program activities.
  • Ensure compliance with PHASE Nepal policies, government requirements, safeguarding and accountability standards.

2. Health Supervisor

  • Supervise and provide technical support to health staff.
  • Coordinate day-to-day health service delivery and outreach activities.
  • Monitor the quality and coverage of health services.
  • Provide and support clinical services, including patient care, safer motherhood and newborn care as required.
  •  Ensure proper HMIS recording, reporting and documentation.
  • Support referrals, community mobilization and emergency health activities.
  • Coordinate with local health authorities, health facilities and relevant stakeholders.

3. Staff Nurse

  •  Provide quality nursing and basic health care services to patients and affected community members.
  • Conduct patient assessment and provide appropriate nursing care and treatment as directed by the responsible health professional.
  • Monitor patients’ conditions and provide necessary follow-up and referral.
  •  Administer medicines and treatments as prescribed and maintain appropriate records.
  •  Provide health education and counselling to patients and community members.
  •  Support health screening, outreach clinics and community-based health activities.
  •  Maintain accurate patient records, registers and other required documentation.
  • Follow infection prevention and control measures and maintain a safe and hygienic service environment.
  • Support emergency health activities and other program activities as required.
  • Coordinate with Health Supervisors, ANMs and other health personnel for effective service delivery.
  • Perform other duties related to the position as assigned by the supervisor.

4. Auxiliary Nurse Midwife (ANM)

  •  Provide basic nursing and community health services.
  • Support antenatal, postnatal, reproductive, maternal and child health services.
  •  Support safe motherhood and newborn care services as required.
  •  Conduct community health education and awareness activities.
  • Identify maternal and newborn danger signs and facilitate timely referral.
  •  Maintain patient records and required documentation.
  •  Support outreach and emergency response activities.
  •  Coordinate with other health personnel for effective service delivery.

General Requirements

Candidates applying for the above positions should:

  • Have good communication, interpersonal and teamwork skills.
  •  Be willing to work in a field-based and challenging environment.
  • Be willing to travel to affected communities and other locations as required.
  •  Demonstrate commitment to safeguarding, protection, gender equality, inclusion and professional ethics.
  •  Be able to work effectively with diverse communities and stakeholders.

Insurance & Benefits

PHASE Nepal will provide accidental insurance coverage of NRs. 20,00,000/- for employees and medical insurance coverage of NRs. 2,25,000/-, covering the employee and up to two dependent family members.

How to Apply

Interested candidates who meet the above-mentioned criteria are requested to submit their application by filling out the application form through the link https://ee-eu.kobotoolbox.org/x/FW7VPgxu no later than 2 October 2026.

PHASE Nepal reserves the right to qualify or disqualify applications at any stage of the recruitment process.

We are urgently looking to fill these positions. Therefore, PHASE Nepal reserves the right to close the vacancy before the stated deadline if suitable candidates are identified. Interested candidates are encouraged to apply as soon as possible.

PHASE Nepal is an equal opportunity employer and strictly follows a merit-based selection process. Qualified women, persons with disabilities and candidates from disadvantaged and marginalized communities are strongly encouraged to apply.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for the further selection process.

No telephone inquiries will be entertained, and any inappropriate recommendation or undue influence will automatically disqualify the candidate from the further selection process.

Position: WASH Facilitator

The WASH Facilitator will support the WASH Officer/Programme Officer in the effective implementation, monitoring, and follow-up of Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) activities at the community level. The position will work closely with community members, WASH committees, local stakeholders, and project staff to promote sustainable WASH practices, strengthen community ownership, and ensure that WASH activities are implemented according to project plans, organizational policies, and relevant standards. Organizational Context

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability.

IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe.

The IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles.

The IFRC is currently present in Nepal through a Country Delegation (CD – first established in 1965 with a presence through regional representation at times), providing support to Nepal Red Cross Society (NRCS) programmes and National Society development (NSD) amongst as well as emergency response, other areas. The longer-term mission of the Nepal Delegation is to facilitate organisational growth, technical capacities, partnerships, and resource mobilisation that enable Nepal Red Cross Society to deliver on its humanitarian mandate in the country through the provision of technical support, advocacy, representation and coordination functions, in accordance with Strategy 2030, the IFRC Renewal and annual Operational Plans.

The Country Delegation also provides integration services to six IFRC members with a presence in Nepal.

On 26 August 2026, a major ice-rock avalanche occurred in the upper Bhote Koshi watershed near the China–Nepal border, resulting in an historically powerful flash flood that advanced from the border down the entire length of Nepal along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli River basins.

Due to the evolving operational requirements of the Rasuwa Flash Flood 2026 response operation, this role profile provides an overview of the principal responsibilities and functions associated with this position within a Federation-coordinated operation.

Job Purpose

Sr. Officer, Communications will coordinate communications and media activities to highlight the humanitarian situation and needs on the ground, as well as the National Society’s response, supported by IFRC and its network, through compelling content on relevant communication channels to reach target audiences. This involves crafting impactful communication key messages about the humanitarian situation in country, outlining the roles of the IFRC network in supporting the host National Society.

Additionally, the role involves enhancing the visibility and public image of the host National Society and IFRC, with a specific focus on emergency and crisis responses, in the international media. The role holder will create or commission high-quality communication materials that give a voice to populations affected by disasters and crises, showcasing the impact of the host National Society’s operations and programmes, contributing to resource mobilization efforts and reporting to partners and stakeholders.

Sr. Officer, Communications also supports the host National Society in coordinating communication activities within the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement, including the development of key messages for public advocacy. Furthermore, the incumbent will provide technical assistance and support to the NS in further developing and strengthening their communication capacity and systems.

Job Duties and Responsibilities

Sr. Officer, Communications is responsible for supporting the NS and the wider network through:

  • In collaboration with the host National Society, develop and implement a communications strategy and plan of action, that supports programmatic and policy priorities, covering the various aspects of communications including public and media relations, corporate communication, social media, and advocacy.
  • Coordinate the production of communication products to support IFRC network advocacy, marketing, and fundraising efforts.
  • Create human interest stories, high-quality photography and videography materials to support donor reporting.
  • Develop and update external-facing key messages for use by IFRC and the wider Red Cross and Red Crescent communications network. Share any communications material created with the IFRC communications team for wider distribution and use among the IFRC communications network.
  • Ensure strong visibility in international media through producing stories and content pitching story ideas about Red Cross and Red Crescent operations. Arrange media visits to field operations, act as a spokesperson (when applicable) with international media, ensure the availability of in-country well-briefed spokespeople for media. Produce communication materials for media and external audiences and support the IFRC/NS
  • spokes persons in media engagements.
  • Ensure strong social media engagement through proposing and producing content for IFRC channels such as Facebook, Instagram and X and tracking audience engagement with social media.
  • Ensure comprehensive and effective communication of major milestones for the emergency response using diverse people-centered content, including video footage, photos with extended captions, and content generated by community engagement activities, such as feedback/concerns from affected communities.
  • In coordination with the IFRC technical focal persons, create high quality content demonstrating the positive impact on affected populations of programmes and operations implemented by the host National Society with the support from IFRC, for further resource mobilization, reporting and general profiling and awareness raising purposes.
  • Work closely with the host National Society and the IFRC regional/in-country Strategic Partnership and Resource Mobilization focal point to create materials that support resource mobilization interventions.
  • Support the host National Society in the coordination of media and communications initiatives among the Movement partners to ensure an aligned Movement approach to public communications, and consistent messaging including coordination of key messages, reactive lines, where required, for different situations.
  • Facilitate visits/ field trips by media, Partner National Societies’ (PNS) communicators.
  • Supporting the management of reputational issues through monitoring, advising on, and responding to developments and issues with possible reputational consequences in close coordination with the Head of Delegation and the Risk Management delegate/focal point.
  • Supporting the capacity-building of the host National Society’s communications team, including through providing opportunities for learning, coaching, skills transfer, mentoring and facilitation of peer-to-peer exchanges, in coordination and collaboration with the IFRC regional and country team.
  • Coordinate with PNS bi-lateral and multilateral communications teams in-country
    .

Other

  • Under the direction of the line manager, support the annual strategy and work plan of the IFRC Country Delegation Communications as well as the IFRC Global Communications strategy
  • As applicable, mentor the NRCS communication team in relevant fields of communication (social media, website, exposure stories, media engagement, etc.).
  • Coordinate with the Country Delegation team, NRCS team and IFRC Asia Pacific regional team in ensuring consistency of IFRC image is maintained
  • Ensure all IFRC communications activities including the IFRC members in Nepal are well-coordinated with NRCS while also contributing to the enhancement of their capacities.

Education

Experience

Required:

Child Safeguarding Level 3 – the responsibilities of the post holder may require having a regular contact with or access to children or young people because the position holder works in the implementation of the country programme and are visiting programme frequently.

ROLE PURPOSE:

Save the Children is the leading independent organization for children. We save children’s lives; we fight for their rights; we help them fulfill their potential. We work together, with our partners from civil society and government, to inspire breakthroughs in the way the world treats children and to achieve immediate and lasting change in their lives.

The Senior Coordinator – FSL and CVA will provide technical oversight, coordination, regular FSL and market situation update and reporting for food security, livelihoods, Cash and Voucher Assistance, and early recovery interventions within the emergency response and recovery. The position will ensure that affected households and communities receive timely, appropriate, and evidence-based support to address immediate food needs while strengthening recovery of livelihood. The role will support in assessments, programme design and take lead in implementation, coordination, monitoring, and recovery planning in accordance with humanitarian standards and organizational priorities.

SCOPE OF ROLE:

Technical Reporting: Livelihood Specialist

KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY:

  • With guidance support from Livelihood Specialist, take lead field assessments of food security and livelihood needs among affected households and communities to identify priority populations, geographic areas, vulnerabilities, market situation and response gaps.
  • Assess the impact of the emergency on different aspects of livelihoods such as household income, markets, agriculture, livestock, and other productive livelihood assets.
  • Collect, analyze and regularly update data on food security conditions, livelihood disruptions, coping mechanisms, market functionality, and community priorities.
  • Contribute sector-specific information and analysis to situation reports, humanitarian assessments, and program planning processes.
  • Conduct market assessments to determine the feasibility of Cash and Voucher Assistance (CVA) in flood-affected areas across SCI interventions where CVA is considered an appropriate delivery approach.
  • From market assessment finding, recommend appropriate CVA interventions modality useful across SCI CVA programming.
  • Provide technical guidance on the transition from immediate food-security assistance to livelihood recovery and to development
  • Ensure FSL interventions are evidence-based, inclusive, gender-responsive and appropriately targeted to the most vulnerable households and contributing to children’s wellbeing.
  • Participate actively in relevant FSL Cluster meetings, technical working groups, and coordination forums organized at field level and ensure Save the Children’s progress update
  • Support joint assessments, analyses, and response planning initiatives with partners and coordination bodies.
  • Regularly collect local market information and provide update in situation and progress update meeting
  • Strengthen collaboration and information sharing among stakeholders to maximize response effectiveness and avoid duplication.
  • Provide technical guidance, and mentoring to field teams, partners, and community-based groups involved in food security and livelihood interventions.
  • Support to build staff and partner capacity on food security and livelihood assessments, livelihoods programming, market-based approaches, CVA, and emergency response standards.
  • Ensure programmes uphold the dignity, rights, and safety of affected individuals and communities.
  • Ensure FSL is integrated across the wider humanitarian response, including education, child protection, WASH, health & nutrition and shelter/settlement, and other sectoral interventions.
  • Ensure field information is collected using approved tools, formats, and reporting templates.
  • Verify information from multiple sources before sharing with internal and external stakeholders.

All types of fraud, bribery, and corruption must be prevented, including where it benefits the organisation (SCI).

SKILLS AND BEHAVIOURS (our Values in Practice)

  • Holds the team and partners accountable to deliver on their responsibilities – giving them the freedom to deliver in the best way they see fit, providing the necessary development to improve performance and applying appropriate consequences when results are not achieved
  • Sets ambitious and challenging goals for themselves and their team, takes responsibility for their own personal development and encourages others to do the same

  • Values diversity, sees it as a source of competitive strength

Collaboration:

EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS

  • Strong technical expertise in emergency food security, livelihoods, and market-based programming with key expertise on CVA
  • Experience coordinating with government authorities, humanitarian coordination mechanisms, and partner organizations.
  • Strong experience in assessments, analysis, reporting, and information management.
  • Knowledge of international child protection frameworks, safeguarding standards, and humanitarian principles.
  • Ability to travel extensively to flood-affected and remote locations.
  • Fluency in English and Nepali, both written and spoken
  • Ability to collect and verify information under tight deadlines.

The Position plays a leading role in ensuring awards are well managed, donor compliance requirements are met, and organizational standards are upheld. The position works closely with Operations, PDQI, and Finance teams on reporting, monitoring, analysis, and compliance-related processes.

In the event of a major humanitarian emergency, the role holder will be expected to work outside the normal role profile and be able to vary working hours accordingly.

SCOPE OF ROLE:

Reports to: Senior Awards Manager

Staff reporting to this post: N/A

Budget Responsibilities: N/A

Role Dimensions:

External: This position will work with SCI Members, Involvement with international agencies, Consortium Partners and local partners will be required.

Internal: Coordination and consultation with other departments for effective program implementation, planning, thematic integration and execution required.

KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY :

Award Management and Portfolio Planning

  • Ensure that the managed portfolio follows the standard award management systems and processes and that key controls are in place to support effective portfolio management and compliance with donor requirements.
  • For every award, ensure that award management standards management are met.
  • Support the Senior Awards Manager to analyze information on CO’s portfolio analysis.
  • Ensure regular award monitoring exists across the portfolio and monitor spend through participation in BvA meetings to ensure individual award performance is being tracked effectively.
  • Provide regular management information to the Senior Awards Manager on the performance of the allocated portfolio.
  • Support the Senior Awards Manager in the implementation of plans to address any performance issues identified through management information and KPI results.
  • Facilitate regular meetings with key stakeholders in individual award review meeting to ensure that risks and issues are being recognized and action taken.
  • Plan and coordinate field visits to support programme teams and Partners to facilitate award implementation, management and review.

Reporting, Monitoring and analysis

  • Lead the report review and submission process.
  • Provide coordination support to report review processes, ensuring all staff inputs happen in timely and effective manner.
  • Co-ordinate with respective budget holders in order to ensure consistency between narrative and financial reports.
  • Provide advice on donor compliance requirement to program teams on a regular basis to ensure that reports meet donor requirements and format.
  • Review reports and provide feedback to the program team to ensure that reports are of high quality, delivered on time and supported by auditable records.
  • Ensure that member and donor feedback are addressed effectively and in timely manner.
  • Be accountable for the reporting performance of the Country Office through successful negotiation in setting reporting deadlines, dissemination of information and follow up with concerned departments on both timeliness and quality.
  • Provide regular and constructive feedback to program and finance team on quality of reports.
  • Support in training/capacity building on reports writing as required including partners.
  • Adherence to the reporting due dates/deadlines and conduct follow ups with relevant departments.
  • Critical review of programme budgets to identify budget lines for review or omitted costs.
  • Financial analysis skills to perform award monitoring processes, highlight financial issues to Budget Holders and perform further analysis to resolve issues identified.
  • Knowledge of donor budgeting formats to support budget holder understanding.
  • Support in training/capacity building on reports as required including partners.

Coordination:

  • Lead and coordinate award kick off meetings to ensure that all award information is shared effectively with relevant staff, including field offices and partners.
  • Effective and prompt communication with members on their awards and work with other departments to liaise with SC Member offices as and when required.
  • Work with the PDQI and POD in BvA reviews, programme meetings and other departments to develop donor ready narrative and financial reports.
  • Lead and coordinate close-out process and work with departments and Members to ensure awards are closed out on time.
  • Coordinate with donor auditors as necessary and support Finance department.

Compliance (systems, process, donor):

  • Clear understanding of SCI processes and key donor requirements, and support teams across CO to ensure all opportunities, proposals, contracts and amendments follow SCI processes.
  • Ensure that all appropriate donor formats are available in-country and staff have a clear understanding of donor requirements/expectations throughout the award cycle.
  • Ensure potential issues and amendment requests are flagged promptly to the Senior Awards Manager, then to donors via the relevant member.
  • Support Senior Awards Manager to prepare donor waiver/derogation requests.
  • Ensure all AMS records are an accurate reflection of current award status at all times, and have all required documentation attached.
  • Ensure all partners and sub-award agreements undergo legal vetting, are input into and approved through AMS, and work with relevant staff to ensure relevant donor requirements are understood by implementing partners (this may include capacity building).
  • Ensuring that all proposals, contracts and amendments are appropriately authorized including of partners, that new awards documentation is properly registered and updated on AMS and that any issues with the award management system are addressed promptly and effectively.

Partnership and Partner Award Agreement (PAA) management:

  • Support program staff to comply with Save the Children’s Partnership policies and procedures. Work closely with the Senior Awards Manager to ensure that all staff have an understanding of the partnership award templates and that these are used consistently for all partners and sub awards.
  • Review PAA of Partners and provide input as required, ensuring that all necessary documents and annexes are received and recorded on AMS.
  • Ensure that all PAA are approved through AMS system prior to signing of contracts.
  • All partners and PAA are timely created and approved on AMS.
  • Ensure that all adequate attachments are received and recorded on AMS and are retained as part of the award documentation policies.
  • Lead sub award close-out, helping Budget Holders to ensure all tasks are completed as per the close-out checklist and that all required close-out documentations are recorded on AMS.
  • Provide support and work with Partnership Unit and Field Offices to ensure smooth management of sub-awards throughout the life cycle of award.

Safeguarding and Counter Fraud obligation:

We need to keep children, adult at risk and community safe. The position holder is responsible to ensure that they:

  • Take all necessary and appropriate steps to prevent abuse, exploitation, neglect, harm and modern slavery within their areas of responsibility, and in the way they conduct themselves, report and respond to all incidents and concerns whether online or in person, and comply with the Safeguarding Policy and Procedure.
  • Take all necessary and appropriate steps to prevent fraud, bribery, and corruption within their areas of responsibility, report and respond to all incidents and concerns and comply with the Counter-Fraud, Bribery and
  • Corruption Policy and Procedure. All types of fraud, bribery, and corruption must be prevented, including where it benefits the organisation (SCI).
  • Collaborate with safeguarding and counter fraud teams to follow up on donor queries.
  • Understand and implement safeguarding and counter fraud related donor requirements.

Occasional Significant Duties

  • Supporting Save the Children’s dual mandate of development programmes as well as in emergency preparedness and response for children.
  • Represent SC within national and international agencies for as per need including field work
  • Fulfill additional tasks as and when called upon.

BEHAVIOURS (Values in Practice)

Accountability:

holds self accountable for making decisions, managing resources efficiently, achieving and role modelling Save the Children values
holds the team and partners accountable to deliver on their responsibilities – giving them the freedom to deliver in the best way they see fit, providing the necessary development to improve performance and applying appropriate consequences when results are not achieved.

Ambition:

  • sets ambitious and challenging goals for themselves and their team, takes responsibility for their own personal development and encourages their team to do the same
  • widely shares their personal vision for Save the Children, engages and motivates others
  • future orientated, thinks strategically and on a global scale.

Collaboration:

  • builds and maintains effective relationships, with their team, colleagues, Members and external partners and supporters
  • values diversity, sees it as a source of competitive strength
  • approachable, good listener, easy to talk to.

Creativity:

  • develops and encourages new and innovative solutions
  • willing to take disciplined risks.

Integrity:

  • honest, encourages openness and transparency; demonstrates highest levels of integrity

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Master’s Degree in Management or related discipline with 3 years (2 years for GSI group*) experience in development field preferred or bachelor degree with 5 years (2 years for GSI group*).

EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS

Essential

  • Knowledge of the requirements of the major donors and experience in reporting to donors
  • Problem solving skills to identify and lead the resolution of issues
  • Good attention to detail and analytical skills
  • Computer literate (i.e. Word, advanced Excel, Outlook, financial systems).
  • Patient, flexible, able to improvise and communicate clearly and effectively under pressure
  • Excellent planning, management and coordination skills, with the ability to prioritize workload comprised of varying and changing tasks and responsibilities
  • Basic understanding of operational programming, including the realities of the context
  • Strong communication (written and spoken), and interpersonal skills in English, with experience in managing multicultural teams

Desirable

  • Experience of staff management, supervision and capacity building

Additional Job Responsibilities:

The duties and responsibilities as set out above are not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to carry out additional duties within reasonableness of their level of skills and experience.

Equal Opportunities:

The role holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with the SCI Equal Opportunities and Diversity policies and procedures.

Safeguarding obligation:

We need to keep children, adult at risk and community safe. The position holder is responsible to ensure that his/her conduct is in line with the SCI’s Safeguarding policies. Hence our selection process includes rigorous background checks, reflects our commitment to the protection of children, adult at risk and community from abuse, exploitation, and harassment.

Health and Safety:

The role holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with SCI Health and Safety policies and procedures.

Safeguarding our Staff:

The post holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with the SCI anti-harassment policy.

Counter Fraud

The role holder is required to take all necessary and appropriate steps to prevent fraud, bribery, and corruption within their areas of responsibility, report and respond to all incidents and concerns and comply with the Counter-Fraud, Bribery and Corruption Policy and Procedure. All types of fraud, bribery, and corruption must be prevented, including where it benefits the organisation (SCI).

The Organisation

We employ approximately 25,000 people across the globe and work on the ground in over 100 countries to help children affected by crises, or those that need better healthcare, education and child protection. We also campaign and advocate at the highest levels to realise the right of children and to ensure their voices are heard.

We are working towards three breakthroughs in how the world treats children by 2030:

  • No child dies from preventable causes before their 5th birthday
  • All children learn from a quality basic education and that,
  • Violence against children is no longer tolerated

We know that great people make a great organization, and that our employees play a crucial role in helping us achieve our ambitions for children. We value our people and offer a meaningful and rewarding career, along with a collaborative and inclusive workplace where ambition, creativity, and integrity are highly valued.

Application Information

Please apply using a cover letter and up-to-date CV as a single document. Please also include details of your current remuneration and salary expectations.

We need to keep children safe so our selection process, which includes rigorous background checks, reflects our commitment to the protection of children from abuse.

All employees are expected to carry out their duties in accordance with our global anti-harassment policy.

Save the Children does not charge a fee at any stage of the recruitment process.

Company Description

The Why: NEPAL aspires to graduate from least developing country to a lower middle-income country by 2026. However, the development community’s excessive focus today on socio-political empowerment has not yielded the desired economic transformation. In reaching the 2026 national target, shall we wait for institutions of power to become accountably productive or shall we bolster innovations of people to bring inclusive prosperity? And, shall we strengthen grassroots-government collaboration in shaping an equal and enterprising future?

The How: DAAYITWA, with a focus on economic empowerment, envisions an enterprising Nepal where every youth has opportunities for a prosperous future. Daayitwa is a part of the Daayitwa Abhiyaan which consists of four organizations: Daayitwa, Governance Lab, Nepal Leadership Academy based in Nepal and Nepal Rising (Daayitwa-US) based in the U.S. Inspired by shared values of innovation, collaboration, and service, it promotes the socio- economic development of Nepal. The movement fosters inclusive and equitable economic growth by accelerating grassroots innovations, strengthening government institutions, and revitalizing a virtuous cycle of democracy and development through grassroots-government collaboration.
